docs.t:
Abu dhabi 
9th April, Forenoon, 3rd to go, Lt. gen Raj Shukla Sir board
DAF Keywords: NOTHING ASKED SO IMMATERIAL 
 
C: Good morning, read out my name. Where are you from? 
Why is India not moving ahead in Renewables?
(i talked about generation v/s installed capacity)
Yes, so why this issue?
(talked about intermittency, storage etc)
This is all smart language, tell me ground reasons? (I, as an electrical engg spoke more of technical issues, but probably he as an ex-military person wanted more geopolitical and China-factor response)
So are these schemes, INDCs and all false promises? 
(Then to and fro conversation about renewables and EVs; compared landscape in India v/s Europe, US, China)
(then he guided the conversation to IMPORT DEPENDENCE OF CRITICAL MINERALS from china) 
So what should India do about this import issue?
So what is this Pax Silica and what is its aim ?
But in the current Trump scenario, do you think it is trustable?
Okay thank you.

M1 (lady): (Probably an academician, wanted to talk about theoretical concepts of Science. 
But a warm person)
You want to become IFOS, you must know Plant biology? (I clarified I have studied Biology till 10th and then Forestry for the exam)
Why did you not pursue Biology after 10th?
What is timber made up of, biologically? (then discussion about fibres, cells, xylem, phloem etc )
How do plants grow?
How do plants make food?
What is photosynthesis? How do you describe it?
How are plants able to do photosynthesis? 
You want to become an IFOS, what do you know about the nature of duties?
Do you think you will be able to do it? 
How many Biosphere reserves in India?
Name the one (BR) in Arunachal Pradesh
Have you played any sport?
(Yes ma'am swimming)
Any competition you have been to? (yes...)
Okay

M2: (wanted very specific stuff)
Which species of trees India is producing for Economic purposes?
(I listed some 5-6 for timber, paper, bat etc)
You missed sandalwood. Ok so there is another species like sandalwood used in perfumery. What is it? (Agarwood)
How does it work.. What happens in it? Where is it found in India?
What is special about the Indian rhino? How is it different from African rhino?
Name rhino sanctuaries of India 
Why are rhinos poached? 
Horn factor aside, tell me why is it easier to poach a rhino compared to an elephant? 
Now tell speciality about “Rajasthan dress”
You missed “Safa” (pagdi) what is special about it and what colour safa is found in what part of Rajasthan? 
What minerals are found in Rajasthan? 
A new mineral was discovered.... (I could not understand his pronunciation and it 
was a weird and new mineral, so I said sorry idk)
(Still he went on to ask) I will tell the district, you tell me where exactly in that district this mineral is found? (Sir idk the mineral discovery news sorry)
Ok thank you 

M3: (probably Ifos- was more inclined towards telling than asking)
Hmm chemistry optional. You must have studied it recently as the exam was quite recent. What are noble gases? 
Why are they noble?
What are gaseous elements in AQI?
What is their unit?
(I said micro grams per metre cube but he said it is ppm) 
What about of unit of PM? (I said micro grams per metre cube for concentration and micron for size)
Some sports other than Cricket and Hockey in which India is doing good at International level? (I started speaking Badminton, Shooting and then he interrupted and said Archery, wrestling, boxing...)
IFOS is an All India Service. What are the other 2? 
What is the difference between AIS and Central Service?
So do you think you will work with states or centre in AIS?
Do you think you can also get to other departments than Forest? What do you know about it?
You can also work with the Centre in AIS, what do you think? 
What are the 3 Internationally recognized categories of forests? 
What is the Forest working plan and management plan? ( The  he went on to speak about working plan, working scheme, annual plan of operations)

C: Thank you, All the Best.
Observations, acknowledgement and inferences:
Unable to recall some other theoretical questions 
There was “nothing” from my DAF at all except “random” Rajasthan stuff.
Even very typical areas like Aravali, GIB were not discussed 
Only the lady member had some expressions. Quite nice and warm. 
The 2 male members were very neutral face, not very clear enunciation and low volume level. 
O2O: special thanks to Mahesh Bhagwat sir for extensive preparation guidelines & topics and Kartikeyan sir (Vajiram) for thorough discussions and much needed moral support. Ayush sir (Forum) for critical behavioural tips. 
Offline mocks: Samkalp, Forum, Vajiram, Shankar Delhi
Online mocks: Samkalp panel, Samkalp in-group, Upwise, Shankar Chennai, Hornbill 
Actual interview was very different from mocks, more discussion oriented, lesser speaking time, more interruptions; when Shukla sir said to my keywords “those reasons are smart English, tell me ground reasons”, i quickly adapted to precise and simpler language and tone with less keywords
Do watch your mock recordings and prepare their answers as many theory questions were asked directly

Q. In the Third Battle of Panipat, was the Marathas’ fall related to leadership position or military position?
There were several factors. The first factor is that there was the military factor. There was lack of technical upgrade or the guns or artillerys which the other parties possessed such as Ahmad Shah Abdali. Secondly, the diplomatic factor was there as well. For example, the Marathas were not able to forge alliances with the Rajputs or other communities. Moreover, the lack of second-rung leadership during the battlefield. During that time when the leadership of Peshwa fell, there was no second-rung of leadership, leading to chaos in the battlefield, which ultimately led to the decline of Marathas in the Third Battle of Panipat.

Safety and cleanliness would be the first perspective because tourism would thrive only if people are not mere spectators but are gracious hosts. UPSC Interview Transcript

Board: Sheel Vardhan Sir
Date: 12/02/2026- Afternoon

Keywords: Sindhudurg, Maharashtra, Cashew Farming, Kathak, Lavani, Writing Quotes and Poetry, Electronics and Telecommunication Engineering, Sociology, MIT Pune, Magazine Editor, Cultural Club Head

I entered the board and greeted all the members.
---

Chairperson

1. Your name has a connection with ancient literature. Do you know about this?

2. What about the Aranyakas and the Upanishads?

3. You were an editor for a college magazine. Do you read newspapers?

4. I am making a statement. Can you elaborate on this?

“The sports page of a newspaper reflects the full truth, the editorial page reflects half the truth, whereas the front page reflects minimum truth.”

(Some discussion followed.)

5. As your hobby is writing quotes, tell me one quote that guides you.

I said:
“Try to be a rainbow in someone’s cloud.”

6. How would you be a “rainbow” as a District Magistrate?

7. Which scheme, according to you, has the potential to be a rainbow?

I said VB GRAM G — because poverty is the darkest cloud of all, and the scheme provides dignity and meaningful work opportunities.
(He was nodding and appreciating in between.)

8. Define folk dance.

Member 2 (Lady Member)

1. You perform Kathak. Would you be okay if fusion dance forms are performed?

2. After I replied that as long as the philosophical core principles and techniques remain intact, innovation is acceptable, she again asked:
Would you still be okay with fusion?

3. You are a poet. Are poets observant individuals or social reformers?

4. Give one example to support your argument.

I cited Savitribai Phule and her literary work Bawankashi Subodh Ratnakar.

5. You have studied Sociology. Which concept do you find most useful?

I spoke about Social Facts.

Member 3

1. Taking a cue from the last discussion, did you take Sociology only from an exam perspective?

I explained my rationale.

2. You are an Electronics and Telecommunication engineer. Don’t you think an engineering degree certificate is merely a piece of paper?
(He was nodding in agreement in between.)

3. Why are there so many engineering colleges and high enrolment in states like Maharashtra and Karnataka, especially from a sociological point of view?

I spoke about the rise in aspirations and the preference for professional degrees.

4. He mentioned that in many Western countries, Electrical and Electronics syllabi are integrated, which is not the case in India.
Have you read the Electrical syllabus?

I replied in the negative.
He said, “No issues, it’s okay.”

5. This is a personality test—do you want us to know you more, or to test you?

I said that I would like them to know me more, and in that process, they would also test me.
(He smiled slightly.)

Member 4

1. You perform Lavani. It is a very energetic dance form. What does Lavani express?

2. What do you like about this dance form?

3. Suppose you help someone, but that person is neither grateful nor reciprocative. How would you express this through Lavani?

I said that I would first need to write a Lavani song to express that feeling, but in life, I do not let such experiences affect my helping nature—I continue doing my part.

He said, “Excellent, on that part.”

4. Describe Kanhoji Angre.
(Reference: Sindhudurg Fort)

5. Further discussion followed on the Marathas and his role in shipbuilding.

6. You are engaged in an exciting activity like cashew farming. Why, then, put in such hard work for civil services?( All of them exchanged smile among themselves)

Member 5

1. What is the percentage of protein in cashews?

2. What are the benefits of nuts like almonds and cashews?

3. What is a balanced diet?

4. Are you having a balanced diet these days?

I replied that I had one when I was at home, but since shifting to Delhi, the balance has been disturbed.

5. What is junk food?

6. What are its ill effects?

7. Should we ban all advertisements promoting junk food?

8. What can be done to control the spread of junk food?

9. Define culture.
10. Define Western culture. What are its traits, and why is it called so?

11. Tell me three women from
Maharashtra who inspire you.

I spoke about Savitribai Phule, Sindhutai Sapkal, and K. Majulaxmi (former Collector of my district).

The board member sitting next to him exclaimed, “All women?”
The member clarified that he was specifically asking about women.

12. You have a hobby of writing poems. Do you take time, or can you compose one on the spot?

I said that generally, I take time.

13. Can you write one now?

I asked if I could try writing a quote instead of a poem.
They agreed and allowed me to take my time using pen and paper.

While I was thinking, the Chairperson stood up to drink water. 
When I looked up, he waited and asked if I was ready.

I said, “Yes, sir.”

My quote was:

> “She was smiling because her strength was born out of the storms she survived.”

All members smiled and acknowledged it.
The Chairperson said that it was very quick.

Another member then said in Marathi:
“Jastich kadak zala ka interview?”
( May be he co related the term Storm with the interview )

I was surprised to hear Marathi from him, as I had assumed he was Punjabi (since he was wearing a turban). I asked him again to confirm it, and we smiled.

The Chairperson then said:
“It was great talking to you. You can leave now.”

I thanked them all and left.

It was a conversational interview.
All board member seemed genuinely interested in conversation.

Guidance Taken:

1. One-to-one discussion with Anupam Jain Sir (Smartwork Labs)

He acted as a “calm in chaos,” helping me focus on what was truly needed and not get lost in clutter.

He hand-held me right from deciding the entries to be filled in the DAF.

We had detailed one-to-one discussions on each aspect of my DAF.

He guided me to think in the right direction, which significantly improved the quality and clarity of my answers.

Especially, discussions on my hobbies—particularly writing quotes—helped me a lot.

His trust in me strengthened my self-belief and helped me remain confident during the interview.

2. Pranay Agarwal Sir (IAS Gurukul)

Conducted detailed DAF-based questioning.
Very encouraging overall and helped boost confidence.

3. Mahesh Bhagwat Sir

Helped me prepare DAF-based questions in a more structured and focused manner.

Mock Interviews:

(Arranged from best to average)

1. Maharashtra Sadan (best of them all)

2. Study IQ (Khemka Sir–led panel)

3. Unacademy

4. Chanakya Mandal Pariwar

5. Quantel – SPM Academy

6. Next IAS

7. Vajiram and Ravi

8. Vajirao and Reddy

9. PW Only IAS

10. Sankalp IAS

11. Quantel – Raj Malhotra Institute

Discussions with my peer group helped me improve my expression and gain new perspectives
Best wishes to all! 🌸

Greeted everyone, Ma'am asked me to take my seat.

Ma'am read my DAF and pointed out towards my work experience with an aggregator. 

Ma'am: Are you still working? 
I said no ma'am. (worked till July 2025). 
Ma'am: But you worked for quite sometime here.
I said yes ma'am. 
Ma'am: Is this work related to civil engineering?
I Said no ma'am. It dealt with Time Value of Money. 
She said okay. (i expected a related question as 5 years i did that job)

Ma'am: So, Murphy's Law- Help me understand this. You are a civil engineer, India is a hot climate country yet we have this trend of glass buildings. Why?

(First question itself bouncer for me, given 5+ years gap with Engineering). I couldn't think beyond asthetics.And it wasn't very engineering answer so i didn't said that.
Gave 2 points (1 was horribly wrong)
1. ma'am we also have a lot of dust and it could help in such structures. (realised as soon as those words left my mouth that it was a senseless point). 
ma'am: Dust can be blocked by concrete walls as well. Plus glass gets dirty.
I said Yes ma'am.
2. In some buildings modified glass looking facade is used to act as solar panels as well. 

She nodded , but wasn't fully convinced (as i am sure this wasn't the right explanation)

I then added sorry' ma'am i cannot think of any other engineering justification as of now. (as soon as i saw the first glass building after returning from UPSC bhavan - it struck me; Material costs are key consideration here since steel is more expensive and is integral to modern concrete constructions so glass does offer little glass advantage by limiting use of steel and concrete to just frame)

Ma'am: Okay tell me what are Green buildings.

I said, buildings that are sustainable. Both- during their construction - using low carbon process and materials, as well as during their operations and life cycle.

Ma'am: Tell me some elements of Green buildings. Assuming construction phase has used sustainable process.

I said: 1. Clean air conditioning and heating. 2. Using Footsteps and activities in the building to generate some power. 3. Treating and re-using Grey Water. 
Ma'am interjected and asked- Treated water, meaning rain water harvesting?
I said ma'am Rain water harvesting is a part, but by Grey water -i mean - water from toilets being treated and re used for non drinking purposes like gardening and cleaning.

She seemed convinced.

Ma'am: So you live in Jharkhand. Must have heard about Jamtara. How do we prevent such things if you are posted in any district of Jharkhand?

I said - Ma'am the people involved in Jamtara were mostly footsoldiers. And operated at behest of outside criminal networks  like the ones in south east asia. So awareness will be a key tool in combating.

I said we don't have that luxury of that cooperative America at the moment but we should practice the strategy of building strength and bide our time. 

Sir added something more - about that Chinese strategy and said you should read more about this. I said right sir.

M3: Sir started conversation in Hindi 
आप civil engineer हैं। (I dreaded again 🫠)
देखिए मेरे पिताजी ने एक घर बना कर दिया उसमें ही मै रहता हूं।  मैं एक ग़रीब आदमी हूं नया घर नहीं बना सकता। हमारे घर में सीलन की समस्या है। आप बताइए बिना पैसे खर्च किए कैसे इस समस्या को दूर किया जाए? 
आप समझते हैं न सीलन क्या है? 
(Although i had planned in mocks to keep my mode English, still it felt like I should ask because we were sitting on a small dining table type setting unlike mocks- where it felt more formal)

I Said - sir shall i continue in English or answer this in Hindi?

Sir -  आपको तो हिंदी अच्छे से आती होगी, हिंदी में ही बात करिए।

मैंने कहा - जी सिर। सीलन घर के नीचे वाली मिट्टी में पानी के कारण होती है (और दीवार और छत पर भी पानी की वजह से)

मेरे अनुसार अगर हम Lime (चुना) treatment करें घर के नीचे वाली मिट्टी की  तो वह मिट्टी डिहाइड्रेट होजाएगी। 

sir ne bola - घर तो बना हुआ है कैसे घर के नीचे वाली मिट्टी में लाइम ट्रीटमेंट करोगे । ( I didn't wanted to push back here- as he might have something pre set in mind)

मैंने कहा - सिर वॉटरप्रूफ पेंट लगा सकते (for walls)

Sir said- भाई इसमें तो पैसे खर्च हो जाएंगे। मैं गरीब हूं।

I said- माफ़ करिएगा sir मैं अभी और कुछ तरीके नहीं सोच पा रहा।

Sir in very jolly mood said; घर के चारो और की मिट्टी काट दें अगर कुछ दूर तक तो हो जाएगा काम. ( I thought in my head - how the hell will it not cost money, isse accha to lime hi daal lete- sasti hoti h)

I said; जी सर।

Sir - आपका जन्म स्थल गया है।गया हिंदुओं के लिए काफी महत्वपूर्ण माना जाता है। फल्गु नदी और उसके आसपास पहाड़ों पर के मंदिर। क्यूं?

I said: जी सर। गया काफ़ी महत्वपूर्ण हैं। यह पिंडदान के लिए काफ़ी प्रसिध्द है। पितृपक्ष में यहां काफ़ी लोग पिंडदान करने आते है अपने पूर्वजों के लिए। 

Sir: क्यों?
सर ऐसा माना जाता है कि अगर आप गया में पिंडदान करते है तो आपको पितृऋण से मुक्ति मिलती है! श्री राम और सीता जी ने दशरथ जी के की गया में ही पिंडदान किया था।

Sir - विष्णुपद मंदिर के बारे में बताइए क्या है ऐसा?

I said; सर ऐसा माना जाता है कि गया शहर गयासुर नाम के राक्षस के ऊपर बसा हुआ है। और जब भी वह अस्थिर होते थे तो शहर v अस्थिर हो जाता था। तो भगवान विष्णु ने उनके छाती पर अपने एक पांव रख दिए जिससे वह शांत हो गए। और जहां पर भगवान विष्णु के पांव पड़े थे वहीं पर उनके पद के निशान बन गए। 
इसके लिए ही विष्णुपद के नाम से जाना जाने लगा।

Sir: अच्छा ये बताइए। आप ऐसा देख रहे होंगे आजकल परिवार छोटे हो गए हैं। पहले हम सब एक छत के नीचे रहते थे अब सब अलग अलग। ऐसा क्यों हो रहा है । जब हमारे पास पैसे नहीं होते थे तो परिवार जुड़ा हुआ था,अब परिवार टूट रहे हैं आपका क्या विचार है?

I said; सर मेरा मानना है कि परिवार टूट नहीं रहे मगर "Transform"  हो रही। (Couldn't think of hindi word for transform then) 

आजकल नौकरी एवं अन्य कारणों से लोगों को migrate करना पड़ रहा। इसके अलावा अब घर में दोनों व्यक्ति (पति पत्नी) काम करते हैं। तो यह ज़रूरत भी बन चुकी है।

इसके बावजूद हम अपने परिवार से जुड़े रहते हैं। मुलाकात होती रहती है। बात होती रहती है। और जबतक यह सौहार्द का भाव रहेगा परिवार टूटेंगे नहीं। 

Sir nodded and moved on to next  question।

आप Politcal साइंस के विद्यार्थी हैं (Optional) भारत में 2-4 Century BC se democratic culture hai। Kuch 3-4 aise गणराज्य ke naam bataie। 

( I felt more than PSIR it was ancient history) 

 मैंने कहा 

मगध 
अंग
वैशाली 

Sir- वैशाली तो नहीं है। I said sorry sir मैं अभी सोच नहीं पा रहा और नाम। (I easnot sure what all were Republics- otherwise would have continued with Vaji, Ujjain etc)

Next- 

  अच्छा ये बताइए - भारत में काफी प्रसिद्ध विश्वविद्यालय थे ; नालंदा एवं विक्रमशिला। आप जानते हैं कौनसे डिस्ट्रीक्ट में है विक्रमशिला। 

मैने कहा ; जी भागलपुर।

Sir- अब ये बताइए इन दोनों में पढ़ाने के तरीके में क्या अंतर था? (  I felt lost- prelims k baad Ancient history aiss hi yaaad nahi rhti- maybe related to different type of Buddhism - but i had no Idea)

Said- Sorry sir.  मुझे इसका ज्ञान नहीं।

सर ने कहा कोई बात नहीं। Ma'am then indicated next member 

M4:
So you are a civil engineer (🥲) 

We observe this issues of poor construction quality.  Why is it that we have poor quality compared to British era structures.

I Said - sir one prime reason that i can think of is we follow Project based approach in india. where demand for engineers peak during construction phase. 

On the other hand the idea should be to have life cycle based approach. Where engineers are engaged throughout the life cycle of any structure not just construction. It is followed in developed countries. 
I added NHAI has started doing it. 

Then he started talking about the bridges - Indore, Mumbai and added in Bihar it's common for bridges to fail.

I said - Sir in the context the Bhopal 90degree Bridge (sir said yes Bhopal). Bridges do not get constructed in matter of days. it takes 2-3 years. And there is usually regular audit. It seems it was not properly done otherwise the issue would have been flagged. 

So who do you hold accountable? The contractor would say i am executing the design given. 

I said, sir we need to identify at what levels lapses have been there. Right from design to execution and audit. And need to  fix accountability at every level.

Then again - Why does it happen? 

I said we also have very high tolerance for non compliance in some areas.
(Ma'am raised eyebrows with a grin -and the sir who asked - other members also changed their facial expressions from smiling poker face to wider grin and maybe mild surprise/shock on me uttering those words)

Sir asked- 

North Bihar is flood prone. Are you aware we are constructing a medical College there. 
I said yes sir- AIIMS Darbhanga.

How do you construct in a flood prone area. 

I said- if we have to construct in a water logged situation; can explore coffer dam to halt water and do the foundation work like we do in case of river bridges.

Sir said - Coffer Dam will last only one year or so then what?
I thought he was referring to overall approach towards structures in flood prone areas.
I said we need to have elevated structures on piers or basement having provision for flood waters to pass as is followed in Japan. However for that there needs to be complete interconnectedness of drainage system in the municipality. ( Maybe he wanted to know about identification of areas which are not in flood plain then do the construction but he didn't follow up)

Sir- What is the process to be followed in construction? Do we just do tendering and start??

I said - Sir we start with feasibility study. For example - if we want to construct a road, need to first asess requirement, traffic studies and see if feasible to construct at that area.

Next do preliminary survey. 
(sir said - something related to one step i can't recall but i had said, yes sir it will be part of feasibility studies)
After that design phase and follow up with tendering, then execution. 

Ma'am said - Thank You your interview is over you can go. I thanked everyone and left. 

I felt that conversation was not long maybe 20minutes. But then
Glanced at clock while getting up from chair - It was 3:35PM. Had not checked the clock while entering (was zoned out) 

Maybe i entered around 3PM as i was escorted 10 -12 minutes before 3PM from waiting area and waited for 5-10 minutes outside. (Don't know time feels different there)  so I guess around 30 minutes 

Asked the person escorting me back - Kinka board tha. He said with surprise - Suman Sharma Ma'am ka. ( am I cooked 🥲?)

Ignorance is bliss 😄🤣. But it made sense. Felt board had an idea what all i could be well prepared as we are in the third phase so no point asking "easy questions" 🥲( budget, Hobbies, Work,  IR) so they leaned towards one weak link- civil engineering (as i had no connection with it for 5+ years and no related work experience) So might have theoretical knowledge of the subject (which i did and had prepared in last 50 days or so-but not other practical aspects)

Fumbled a bit in 2-3 places. 
While answering glanced at others occassionally - everyone was listening. Ma'am was noting down stuff here and there. Some members too. 

Felt very different from mocks. Even questions were not in QnA format but just conversation - so couldn't just go with template made answers. But in hindsight some aspects like; Jamtara , Bihar qs and quality of construction - could have been better tackled (This will always be the regret no matter what)

Very cordial and comfortable board. 

Mocks; Vajiram, Vajirao and Reddy,Vision Ias, Samkalp (2), Sriram IAS, Ekagra IAS, NACS Bihar Jharkhand, CMP O2O 

Peer Discussion with my mains group friends. 
Non UPSC Friends - helped in analysis other aspects through Mock videos feedback.

Trump is talking of such things, and people are taking him seriously. (I said, Sir I think they are taking his actions seriously, and not his words) (Sir made an expressionless face and nodded for a second)

but in interview you may not be able to recall.
All were cordial in the sense that no one was trying to intimidate , you don’t know something , they will ask another question. In my understanding , they want to bring out the best out of you. In case you don’t do well in one question, they will ask another. I think every board member is trying to get something out of you. And they will do it very gently.
In interview take your time ,  there is no hurry , they will give you ample time to think. 
Please don’t judge yourself during the interview, let them do their work and you do yours. 
“Don’t answer , lets just talk”

These are the lessons from my mistakes that I made and what I learnt from that day.
Take this day as any other day and you will do great. Take stress for what may come , you may not do well.
In my journey in CSE prep , I was always rewarded for the efforts I had made. So , believe in yourself , you have what
they want. 

Preparation ; One to One were more helpful , Sajjal sir(Sarrthi) was very considerate guided  me as in how to think and structure the responses ,One to One at Samkalp (mine was not with Shantosh Taneja Sir)  helped me fill gaps , Satyam Jain (UnderstandUPSC) and Vijaya D P Singh (VisionIAS) were helpful and encouraging.

(1/2)
Name : RS
Date : 27/02/2025, forenoon session
Board : Raj shukla (poker face, continuously going out and ringing bells in between) 
DAF key words : AP, Movies, Dogs, IIT X, Civil engineering, Sociology
Time : around 20-25 minutes. 
 
Overall experience : it was completely unrelated to mocks. Nothing based on Current affairs. Round big (dinner)table like setup not seen any where in mocks. More of discussion than QnA. 4/5 members grilled continuously to see if would I change my stance
 1. Chair person 
 a. Long discussion on how customary practices are being increasingly becoming uniform due to modern law. It was at this point I said I don’t know and he said let me finish. This is not QnA, we will have Intelligent discussion. I apologised and let him continue 
 b.  Do you think such modern laws that brings uniformity in customs is necessary ?
 c. How do we resolve such disputes ?
 d. Have you heard of streedhan? 
 e. Can SC be involved in this ? 
 f. Do you know of hindu succession act? And discussion on how bringing uniformity in law is causing troubles in such aspects?
 2. Member 1 
 a. Talked about NEET (30% youth not in education, employment or training). How do we solve this? 
 b. Why govt is not able to provide this? 
 c.  he said people are shifting from one job to another, what could be the reasons ? 
 d. I mentioned something about state govt, he asked why state govts are not able to provide ? 
 e. Follow up on my answer, what is the use of freebies, your take on it? I gave my opinion and said there should be sunset clause to the end. He asked how many years 3 or 4 or 5 or 10 years? I said that should be done based on Cost benefit ratio and party consensus
 f. Discussion on capital expenditure and revenue expenditure, should we have more capex?
 g. All along this while, the chairman continuously rang bell for puine, went out multiple times to see if would be distracted. no matter what, I did not even care for such actions. Just focused on the person I was answering 
 3. Member 2 (very close to my left) 
 a. Greeted hello X, continuing on chairperson discussion, you say there should be balance or should communities themselves resolve this? I said if constitutional aspect of dignity is violated state should intervene, else communities can themselves resolve other matters 
 b. What is your take on Cock fighting that happens during festivals in AP ? Even MPs/MLAs are known to be involved in this, can communities involve in such issues? I said since betting is involved govt should get involved. He then said, remove the gambling aspect, can communities resolve any other issues amongst themselves or should we ban such practices, say even jallikatu? 
 c. How to resolve the issue of stray dogs ? I said stakeholder approach and was continuing, to which he immediately abrupted and said don’t use fancy words, if you are adminstrator what would you do ? 
 d. Since you watch movies, do you justify allu arjun arrest. Was he truly responsible for the stampede? 
 e. In the past too such events happened, can we still arrest them even now? 
 4. Member 3 (close to my right) -she is such a sweet heart. 
 a. Given difference in location of your studies, how different was your school and IIT life especially interms of academics, infra and education? 
 b. What all would you change in your education system, especially in the school you have studied? 
 c. Some discussion on NEP and can it be successful ? 
 d. What is the role of local administration in ensuring the administration of school. I asked if it just the role of MLAs? She said all local administration, to which I gave suited response? 
 e. Role of AI in education? Can it help? 
 f. Isn't there excessive focus on Maths (STEM), what was your experience in school? What should be the focus in future ? 
 5. Member 4 (Had very difficult time in understanding his pronunciations) 
 a. Have you heard about QUAD? 
 b. Is it military alliance? Do you think its Anti china?  (he was pushing me to say it was a military anti china block)
 c. Is it fulfilling its mandate?
(2/2)
d. Given all the global instability, If we go against war with china in indopacific will the neighbours in indopacific come to our rescue? 
 e. Based on my response, he asked what is NAM? Why did we adopt such a philosophy? What is our current policy? 
 f. While our neighbours have elected women as PMs or presidents, india has not been able to do so? What is your take? 
 
Chairman said your interview is over, I thanked everyone and left the place. 
 
All in all, it was a completely different ball game. I went into the place thinking its just another day. This helped me keep my calm. But truth to be told, my heart raced when I was being called to the room. So maintain your calm, don’t get distracted, what people say in mock interviews is not completely relavant. 
 
Mocks given : 2-3 panel mocks (one in hyderabad- the worst, 2 in samkalp- the closest one to interview) 
4 one to one dicussions with : sangamitra maam from Hyderabad, KSG (khan sir), pranay aggrawal sir for sociology and Mridul sir (overall discussions). In my opinion one to one DISCUSSIONS are more better than these artificial panel mocks. Do give 2 of them to be confident or getting used to answering 4-5 elders. 
 
I really thank this telegram channel for its wonderful support mechanism. For those have you who have uploaded, I really thank all of you. It gave a sense of certainty in this uncertain interview. For those, who eagerly see every transcript and yet refuse to share yours, donald trump is less selfish than you people. I leave the rest for you to decide on how low can you take yourself.

The start of my interview was a bit unconventional but then it gained momentum. The board members seemed very interested in my answers. It felt more like a discussion rather than a traditional question answer session.

Mock Interview - Since this my 4th interview. So i attended only 2 mock interview - Samkalp and Chahal. 
Based on my experience I can say that if it is your first interview you should give at least 5-6 interviews to boost your confidence. Otherwise 2-3 interviews are sufficient.

One to One - I attended more 121 than mock interview. 
121 with 
- Satyam Jain - Avoid this.
- Ravindran Sir - Recommended. Discussed variety of question and it will  help you.
- Rahul Sir (ias pcs pathshala) - Highly Recommended. Very much beneficial for structuring and concluding the answer. Sir value addition part was extremely enriching.
- Dharmadhikari Sir - Recommended. Very helpful in confidence boosting.

In a real interview, questions from mock sessions and onetoone discussions will not get repeated but the approach you develop will help you answer random questions. (However I got a bit lucky as 3 questions I had discussed with Rahul Sir were repeated - caste census wala, Bihar-  Jharkhand, and sports section wala🙂)

I believe you should try to articulate your answers in an engaging manner. Avoid giving just 1-2 line responses. Show enthusiasm and eagerness in every answer. Try to cover multiple perspectives using succinct keywords. 

Lastly all the best to everyone and thanking this channel for providing transcript. It was very much helpful 🙏

docs.t:
(1/2) 
INTERVIEW TRANSCRIPT
Interview Date – 30 Jan 2025
Board – Shri Sheel Vardhan Singh 
Forenoon session, 2nd to go. Nearly 45min.
DAF Keywords – Chemical Engineering, Research Internship, Indian Hip Hop Music, Karate, Perspective-taking visualization, Cargill Global Scholars Program, Sociology. 

Chairman
1.  Reads the DAF – You are {Name}, come from {place}. I see that you have mentioned that you follow Indian Hip Hop music, what is it?

2.  From your answer, I see it is more like fusion music rather than a distinct genre of music.

3.  What is the origin of Hip Hop music?
a.  Rooted in protest movement of Afro-Americans during 70s in USA. 

4.  (Building upon my answer) So Hip hop music has this protest element, but Indian Hip hop music lacks this, so how is IHH a category of music?
a.  Gave some examples of tracks that have this element of protest.

5.  What you’re telling is rap music like Tupac Shakur in the west coast etc., is rap same as hip hop?

6.  What do you know about Hindustani music and Carnatic music?

7.  (Interrupts my answer) What is the textual source from which they are derived?
a.  I said sorry sir I’m not aware. Sir said - you know so much about hip hop and western music, you should be aware about our own music as well. 

8.  Our discussion on fusion reminds me of a new genre that is gaining a lot of popularity – Historical fiction. What is your opinion on it?

9.  So according to you it is rooted in history but is essentially fiction?

10.  But I think it is distorting history. When people like Amish write about the people of Meluha, most readers don’t distinguish history from fiction. 
a.  Helps in creating awareness. 
b.  Leads to curiosity about history, people can read more about true history based on their interest.

11.  As per this logic, if there is crime in society, it would create awareness about it amongst people. So, crime is also good for society?
a.  Answered as per normal and pathological social facts of Durkheim and impact on collective conscience. 

12.  So, you have used the Collectivism theory from sociology. What good is this shock to collective conscience? We have seen that in past there have been incidents that have created ripples in society, but the situation remains same and nothing has changed.
a.  I began answering that it depends on the type of crime and the severity. 
b.  (Interrupted in between) I’ll narrow it down for you, let’s talk about crime against women. 

13.  I see in your DAF that you’ve accomplished a lot in research domain. You did {read out the details and achievements}. It seems you were on course to do your PhD, become a professor, do brilliant research and bring in a Nobel Prize for our nation (says this playfully). Why this sudden 180-degree switch to Civil Services?

Member-1

1.  What belt are you in Karate?

2.  Which style of Karate do you practice?
a.  Shito Ryu

3.  Is it related to Shoto-kan? What is the difference between both?

4.  After learning Karate, do you feel like beating people around? Or getting into fights?

5.  So did you not get the opportunity to get into fights or you don’t like it? (with a slight laugh)

6.  Assume that you get into a fight with a random person on the street. He won’t follow the rules that you are taught in Karate like hit above the belt etc. So how would you fight with him?
a.  I mentioned that we are aware of basics of street fighting if someone uses sticks etc. Chairman sir adds that if the person has a gun, then the entire situation changes.
b.  After my answer member says I thought that like my students in exam you would say that this is out of syllabus (starts laughing). He said that I asked these questions to ease you into the interview, now let’s get to serious questions.

7.  You have done Chemical Engineering? There is another discipline called Chemical Technology for graduation. What is the difference between both?

8.  (Probably was not completely satisfied with my previous answer) Can you think of what is the relation between Engineering and Technology?
(2/2)
a.  I said rightly pointed out sir, Technology is actually application of Engineering. I think this was what sir wanted to hear.

9.  Are you aware about Ceramics and related aspects? (I was a little hesitant to answer, so he said you study it as part of your curriculum, right? I said yes)

10.  So at what temperature does ceramic manufacturing takes place?
a.  I said I’m not aware, so sir told roughly around 1500-1800 degree Celsius. 

Member-2

1.  (Asked me to look behind me at the wall) What is it that you see?
a.  National Emblem

2.  Where did it come from?
a.  Mentioned Lion capital from Sarnath Ashokan pillar.

3.  What is the history behind it?
a.  I said I’m unaware. Sir said do read on it, it has very interesting history over the years and especially the British era.

4.  You must be knowing that China claims Arunachal Pradesh as its part, Ladakh as its part. Even Nepal claims Kalapani region as its territory. We Indians have cultural claim to Mt Kailash, we say Lord Shiva even lived there. Why don’t we also start claiming it as our territory? Something of a tit-for-tat response?
a.  Talked about ambition to become Vishwa Guru (Member-4 noted and cross-questioned on this later).

5.  So you’re saying we should be a saint and uphold the global order when we have such a large trade deficit with China? Doesn’t it threaten our sovereignty? 
a.  Cross-question on Chinese FDI incoming.

6.  Where is the Chicken’s neck? 
a.  Where is it located?
b.  It is also known as?
c.  Significance (told this himself)

7.  What district of Bangladesh borders that part? What is the demographic composition of the district?
a.  Told him I’m not aware, said you’re not up to date with this issue. 

Member-3

1.  What is Cargill that you’ve mentioned in your DAF?
a.  Explained the program and what the leadership position was about.

2.  (Clarified) What is Cargill? Is it an organization or name of a person?

3.  You have sociology as your optional. What are Veblen goods?

4.  So, demand increases as the price rises, it that right? How do you explain this phenomenon?

5.  What is India’s policy on Cryptocurrency? Is it legal?

6.  What is President Trump’s stance on Cryptocurrency?

Member-4 (Lady)

1.  You have mentioned that your hobby is Perspective-taking visualizations. What is it?

2.  So how is that a hobby? (looked perplexed)
a.  After my explanation, she looked at Chairman. Sir confirmed by rephrasing it if this is what I mean.
b.  After I said yes sir, ma’am asked sir I’m still not sure how this is a hobby (and started laughing). Sir said this is what he is saying (looked dead serious).
c.  I requested if I could clarify and gave an example. Sir asked if your visualization of your interview going well has manifested (with a smile).

3.  You mentioned about India aspiring to become Vishwa Guru. Don’t you think it is a very ambitious goal?

In order to avoid radically different answer key by UPSC, it's better that on controversial/well debated questions people put representation for most agreed anwers also. A trend has been observed whereby UPSC accepting "minority view answers" while changing original and "majority view answers". 

So better if people represent on both sides, making the Objections Based Alteration system of UPSC more rational and Balanced. 

In nutshell, if people are representing answer A of some question, and 60-70% coachings after much deliberation arrives at conclusion that answer A is correct but few coachings answer key and a good number of aspirants saying answer can be B also based on some random NCERT screenshot or SC judgement etc. and they are filing frequent representation for Answer B. Then it's better that Answer A people also file similar representation so that UPSC don't change answer based on multiple representation received on answer B thinking that it's Rational Approach !

For better understanding deeper ramifications of this, kindly see above data analyses of Previous Answer Keys. After Representation System has been initiated, UPSC Answer Keys has started showing high variations on Coaching Answer Keys as compared to previous years when no such system was there. Especially on few questions which everyone assumes correct but later on UPSC saying otherwise unexpectedly on those questions. All thanks to imbalanced representations on such questions.

Species whose presence or absence indicates the good/bad health of ecosystem. For e.g. - Lichens are good health indicators

As the final result of CSE 2023 is  released recently, just one request to all the toppers/selected candidates of the exam :

Please do take this Coaching Seminar / Interview/Media byte things seriously. Coaching institutes will encircle you like anything soon after results are out and you become GOLDEN DUCKS for them.

There must be some good mentors in the journey who could have helped you to reach the destination. However while accepting/speaking in such coachings keep following few pointers in mind (collected from past toppers experiences)

1. Don't accept request for seminar/interview from commercial coachings if you have not personally genuinely benefitted from it.

2. DON'T accept any cash/ in kind benefits from coachings in lieu of seminars/ toppers talk. They will give you many attracive and seemingly JUSTIFIED in kind gifts/packages etc. But remember there is NO FREE LUNCH in this world plus ETHICS is not over with GS4 exam ! 

3. Write about your journey till now and brief details of all kind of coachings help you took from any institute and whether it benefitted you or not in your previous and present attempt. Share this on all your social media accounts and initial interviews etc because it will act as a great check for future attractive offers for "speaking lies or half-truths" ! Share the message widely post result.

4. Wherever you go speak CLEARLY what all SPECIFIC help you took from the institute like Mains test series or interview mocks only etc Always clearly tell the core truth explicitly in your speech that "BEING GOOD IN ONE THING doesn't mean any coaching is good in all other things also. I have experienced this aspect as good for me so this part I can recommend, not every part which I have not personally experienced."

5. Often core Coaching mentors are important and inspiring persons so there is a MORAL PRESSURE to recommend / say only good thing about him when you are the guest speaker at the place. However remember more than that important pressure is Aspirant / Topper Social Responsibility. Be clear that you are not their Brand Ambassadors ! 

6. Try to share minimal with outside press. And ask clearly to any journalist you are giving a byte to get it first approved from you once before publishing. Otherwise deny it. Warna they will make it a SPICY NEWS benefitting them,not you or aspirants. Experienced by almost all previous toppers. 

7. Immidiately hide/delete all your past social media controversial/political posts/opinions. Make Every personal photos shared in past or future visible to only friends , not open public for some time. Add only friends which you personally know. Rest can live as followers if they want.

Chairperson:
1. How is an upright piano different from a grand piano?
- More compact in size (he asked real differences, to which I said I've no idea)

2. What is the difference between these terms: orthodox, conservative, extremist, terrorist?
- Orthodox: who rigidly applies doctrine; Conservative: who opposes reform; Extremist: who want to persecute non-adherents; Terrorist: who actually ends up doing violence
(Follow up: do you think police can apply such a distinction? I said no bcs it's really difficult to distinguish bw extremists and orthodox)

3. Besides law and civil services, do you read any books? I said Fiction. He asked two most impactful fiction books I've read,. I said Midnight Library (Matt Haig) and Siddhartha (Hermann Hesse). 
- Siddhartha is one of my favorites too. Give a summary of it in three words. (I gave an answer, sir gave another answer which he thought was right. I liked his answer more than mine, frankly)

Member 1:
1. Tell me the differences in European and Indian models of insolvency (I had cursory knowledge which I told them). What about the US model? (I just knew it happens under Chapter 11 Bankruptcy, and liquidation waterfall mechanisms are similar to IBC)

2. What are some conventions on transnational organised crime? (I didn't know any). Have you heard about the UN-CTOC? (I said no)

3. You have worked on game design. Who is the founder of game theory? (I was halfway into saying I don't know when I recalled it was John Nash). 
- when did Nash publish his work? (Probably 1940s-50s, he said yes 50s) 
- Have you read the paper by Nash? (I said no. He said okay, do read it sometime)

4. What is the basis for the Indian Evidence Act?
(I said fair trial, but he asked me to go to the root of the issue, which I couldnt)

- What is the main issue with Evidence Act? Why is it in conflict with Indian ethos?
(there is a significant distrust on individuals and state both, however, many provisions can be dispensed with by giving reasons, and many provisions are not applicable in tribunals. So largely I think it's about safeguards against state excesses and individual deception, not against Indian ethos)

Member 2:
1. What are the changes in CrPC? 
(mandatory forensics, digitised process, higher police custody time frame)
- Why is it under controversy? (I said because of the police custody norms)
- Do you think it is the right step? (I said yes, because accused can abuse the process by going to hospital in first 15 days, so custody needs to be spread out)

2. What are some trends in Left Wing Extremism, how do they continue to organise such mass scale attacks and what can we do?
( I said WHAM strategy has been very effective, LWE districts have come down from 100+ to below 40 lately; covert networks between naxals and villagers continue, which is why they can blend in with the civilians; there's a need to check arms and ammunitions within the domestic regions. Then I said I don't really know what steps are being taken on ground for such a complex issue.)

Member 3:
1. What processes in insolvency are flawed and what need to be changed? (I said it's a great reform but debtor-in-possession needs to be brought back to ensure more timeliness and less erosion of value, and RPs need to be scrutinised more)

2. How many cases are pending in courts? (I said 4cr)

3. Supreme Court wants courts to give bail. So many undertrials are in prison for 10-15 years. (I said there needs to be distinction between police and judicial custody during investigation and after chargesheet is filed. Trial courts shouldnt grant incessant extensions of custody, and police should not be allowed to file supplementary chargesheet)

4. How can we resolve backlog of cases?
(I said firstly, there needs to be an increase in judges. Currently, judge ratio 20 per million, required is atleast 50 per million)
- Is that all?
(No, we need judicial accountability)
- How?
(judges should be answerable for the adjournments they give and delays they cause)
- Should there be a timeline on cases? Is that desirable?
(I said yes. For extreme cases the reasons should be noted in writing for delay and High Court should sit in supervision, otherwise timeline-based action) 

Member 4:
1. How long have you been playing piano? (I said since school, but focused more on bollywood songs since college)
- Then that is merely keyboard, not piano because it's not western classical (I said I have learnt western classical too, a bit)
- Which bollywood song has almost a direct symphony lifted into it? (I said probably Phir Le Aya Dil from Barfi)
- No, have you heard Mozart's 40th Symphony? (I said no) He said listen to it and you'll realise.

2. Why is there so much police brutality in the US? 
(Probably because of low accountability, racial prejudice, risk of gun violence from civilians) 
- why is there so much gun violence in USA? Why don't people listen to the anti-gun lobby? 
(I said 2nd Amendment rights, people want freedom to protect themselves even against state excesses) 
- is the freedom to bear arms meant to be used against the tyranny of the state? (I said yes as far as I recall that's one of the intended reasons) 
- which other countries have right to bear arms but low gun violence? (I said idk, he said take a guess, I said probably countries with conscription like Israel and South Korea, but he said no it's Canada, go see why they don't have such high rates of violence) 

3. Why does police have a bad reputation?
(undertrained and understaffed, custodial violence, rampant petty corruption, selective efficiency)
- Petty corruption? Do you think corruption comes in shades of grey? (I said yes it does, high level political corruption is more dangerous)
- Do you think there should be separate punishments for different degrees of corruption? (I said petty corruption shouldn't be treated with leniency, rather different penalties such as disqualification under RPA or other penalties can be stacked for higher corruption)

4. Have you heard of Oedipus Complex? (yes: no clue how this question arose). 
- What did Oedipus do when he found out he had killed his father and married his own mother? (he blinded himself: I was really unsure if I said it right, but he nodded it was right)
- I will leave you with this parting thought, in light of your answer on petty corruption.

Chairman - Read my DAF aloud.

Why isn't cricket played in China, Japan, and the United States?
2)Are you aware of Parul Chaudhary? Yes, the Gold Medalist. She mentioned that the UP Government has a policy where winning a Gold Medal at the Asian Games qualifies you for a DSP rank in UP. Do you think this is a healthy practice?
3)Can sports be promoted by providing such incentives?
4) Why are there five rings in the Olympics? Can you name all the Indian Olympics gold medalists?

6) In which year was AFSPA enacted? What constitutes a disturbed area under AFSPA?
7) Is there any rationale behind imposing AFSPA today?

Member 1:

1)What is T+1 settlement? Has T+0 settlement been introduced? Doesn't it pose operational complexity? How does SEBI plan to manage it?
2)How many ways are there for a person to acquire Indian citizenship? This leads to a conversation about the Citizenship Amendment Act (CAA). Why is the cutoff date set as 31st December 2014, and what is the debate surrounding it?
3)I noticed you published a research paper on Green Aviation Fuel. Could you explain what it's all about?
4)Tell me Based solely on merit, is India ready for electric vehicles?
5)You seem to be involved in diverse activities. Does that mean you are not focused enough?

Member 2:

1)What kind of work did you do in the NGO? 
2)Do you think NGOs are of no use, and they are here only for namesake?
3)Few questions related to FEMA and transparency.
4)Is there any law in place that allows shoot-at-sight?
5)What is Section 126 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951? Followed by questions on the freebies culture.

Member 3:

1) What is the sex ratio in your state? 
2)Is there any state in India where the female population exceeds the male population?
3)How many colors are there in the national flag? 
4)If it has four colors (saffron, white, green, and navy blue with the Ashoka Chakra), then why is it called Tiranga?
5) How many World Heritage Sites are there in your state? 
6)Despite having huge potential, why is the Indian tourism sector still sluggish? 
7)Is it due to insufficient digital promotion and marketing?
8)With very few players in the aviation market, is it becoming a monopoly of a few? 
9)What are the major challenges facing this sector?

Member 4:

1)What is a semiconductor? 
2)What is the status of semiconductor manufacturing in India? 
3)Can you recall any schemes for semiconductor production?
4)Questions on edible oil import and dependency.
5) Who was the pioneer Bhakti saint of Karnataka? 
6)What qualities do you think we need in today's leaders, inspired by him?
7) why suicide rates are higher in men.
8) What are the differences between homeopathy and Ayurveda? Which is more effective?

Comment - I thoroughly enjoyed the whole process. The board was very cordial. They gave me ample time to think, and the ambiance of the room was very light.

Mock Interview - I took multiple mocks - OnlyIAS, Samkalp, Vajirao, NextIAS. More or less, every coaching mock is the same. They prepare you to handle stressful situations and present yourself in a better way.

One-to-One - S N Patil Sir (DM, my home district) and Rahul Sir (IAS PCS Pathshala). For me, one-to-one sessions were more useful than mocks. Many questions in the interview were on same lines to those Rahul Sir and I had discussed from my DAF. That was very helpful.

Final Thought: To all those going to appear for the interview, I'll give one piece of advice: prepare your DAF very well, as many counter questions can be asked. All the best

Date: 27/03/2024

Entered the room and greeted the lady member and then the males with NAMASKAAR.
M3 said- Your suit looks very good.  Did you buy it readymade or got it stitched? (Sir, I got Stitched)
Chairman- How much did it cost? (10k sir)
Including cloth and stitch? (Yes Sir)
Where did you get it from? ( Sir, Kamla Nagar in Delhi)
Which Shop? (Sir- Raymonds)
OK, tell me what is the fabric quality and thread count of this suit? (I was expecting a bomb question after all the friendly previous convo – I smiled, I do not know about that sir. Thanks for the compliment though.)
He then started reading out my DAF – BSC, MA English, Sociology, Photography, Cycling, NCC, Extempore and Essay Writing. 
What essay did u get a prize for? ( Sir, I wrote an essay on farmer’s suicide)
Don’t you think farmer suicides are overhyped viz-a viz women and student suicides? They do not get any attention?  ( Sir, all suicides are avoidable, but farmer’s distress is largely due to economic reasons. It depicts a deep structural issue that needs to be tackled.)
But student suicides do not get any attention? (Sir they do get attention for eg. Kota suicides and IIT suicides)
How does sociology help in understanding suicide? ( as I started speaking of Durkheim he intervened)
You sociology students for the past 40 years talking of Durkheim only. Do you know of somebody else who has worked on it? (Yes sir. Ramachandra Guha has worked on a study on suicides in India. At this, all members smiled and nodded. Didn't ask anything further)
You have won a prize in extempore as well. What did you speak about? ( Sir, In NCC Camp we were given chits of topics and I got the opportunity to speak on Demonetization)
Was demonetization Good? ( yes Sir, it was a move with good intentions)
What were the reasons? Tell crisply. ( To counter black money, fake currency, terror funding. The hidden benefit was the digitalization of the economy.)
 M1
You are from KUK.( Long Monologue 2-3 minutes)  It's funded by govt. Should we now privatize such institutions? ( Sir, graded privatization can be looked into after due trial. The immediate need is not there)
Why do we need govt institutions? ( high fees in pvt , Development need of the nation for higher education.)
Fees fix kardete h private ki 100 rs. But the volume of students will rise. So it will become profitable. What do you think? ( Smiled, If it is so, their quality will not be up to the mark. Govt will have to subsidize so this is exactly what happens in aided and govt colleges)
Some more questions about this theme... can't recall. 
M3
You are from Haryana. Highlight the participation of Haryana in the war of 1857. ( told factual in the end I said, “I am not very sure but there was some involvement of Ambala Cantonment as well”). I think he wanted to hear Ambala and He started a long monologue on Mangal Pandey, Meerut, Ambala, Barakpore) I could have answered well here. Missed an opportunity. 
Earlier sports policy in Haryana was of giving Policing jobs to medal winners and now we are giving them jobs in the sports department to promote their sport. Which one is good? ( Sir, in those times ‘Padak Lao Nokri Pao’ initiated sports culture in Haryana. This led to the growth of sports complexes and individual games. Current policy is more effective for today as Neeraj Chopra’s talent will be used to train more Olympians.)
 High Per capita income in Haryana yet very high unemployment. Why is this dichotomy? ( People have high incomes, so refuse to work at low wages and due to lack of marketable skills are unemployable. )
What’s the solution? ( two-fold measures – develop capabilities by skill training, quality education and create opportunities by infra development, food processing.....) 
M4
You do photography. Which competitions have you participated in? ( Sir, I am an amateur photographer and like to click pictures. I have not participated in any competition, I am learning.)
You were an NCC Cadet. Give an extempore on NCC. ( Spoke 2 min non-stop on NCC – my forte.)

1. Chairman sir was consistently looking at me with his folded hands below the chin. - stood up once and went to the other side of the room, never interrupted in-between other members to ask questions/cross-questioning himself, only observed.

2. As members asked questions - some smiled looking at each other.

3. As I answered a few questions - M1 often interrupted in-between, I wanted to speak more but as my voice was starting the member (M2) often shifted to the next question.

4. At times in my peripheral view, I saw one two members nodding as I answered questions wrt economy and taxes, some members writing or ticking something on their notepads.

5. I don't know what to say/judge conclusively as most of the questions were opinion based and subsequent discussions. 

Hope for the best 🤞🏼

Then Chair directed the next member to ask

(Mentioned 2018 Kerala floods)

Even after Independence, the trajectory of the two countries were different. (compared between Mao and Nehru). Then asked me to compare between the two countries and two leaders.

docs.t:
Anonymous Warrior:

11.30 am, 1st July 2023. A pdf appeared in one of the chats on my telegram account. This is the last one ever I'll look for my name in - and it was not there. Ten years of my UPSC life which began in 2013 (Manmohan Singh was PM then) came to an end. 

I'll spare you the details of my first five attempts. Mostly failure at preliminary stage - except for once, when I failed at mains stage. 

The final attempt!

In January 2020, I was still contemplating giving the next preliminary exam which would be my last attempt at Civil Services. But then, the pandemic and lockdown happened. With little inspiration from a friend and my now life partner I kick started my preparation once again, behind face masks and among sanitizers.

The preliminary was pushed to October, and I pushed more. I cleared the preliminary (by 0.5 marks as later revealed) and started preparing for main examinations. I corrected some of the mistakes I made in my earlier mains attempt and I was granted an opportunity to visit Dholpur House. I really thought I'm riding my wave. 

But the second wave of Coronavirus pushed the Personality Test to over 6 months. By this time I was exhausted with my preparations. I was also feeling very stressed and anxious that it was my first PT and last attempt. I botched my Interview (which at the time felt okayish). I got one of the lowest PT marks of that year (my written marks were also not great) and once again failed. 

But failure this time felt very different - it was very painful. Because I knew there was no another go at it. My neighbor got IAS and I watched the media visiting from my gate - knowing that it's never going to happen with me now! 

I cried once again. It was hard to keep sane. My mental health took a hit. My now life partner helped me. My friends helped me finally come out of it. Slowly I accepted it and moved on. I started teaching at my friend's academy and dragged on. 

The second final attempt!

I had one Indian Forest Service attempt left in my pocket which I could write latest in 2022 (as I would turn 32 in 2023). I barely cleared CSE prelims cutoffs, so what hope do I have at clearing IFS Cutoffs which is at least 10-15 marks higher.. 
Since I had already accepted that Civil Services might not be my destiny, I didn't prepare for IFS preliminary - I watched a series late into the night before prelims, got up late and went for the exam in a leisurely mood. I was so calm and solving the papers was a sport to me on that day - because I was not expecting to clear it! I just wanted to finish off my attempts and move on in life. 

Yes! You guessed it right - to my absolute surprise I cleared IFS prelims. This time it brought a superstitious belief in me - Life is giving you another opportunity - your dream is going to come true. I had to study two new subjects - Geology and Forestry - which I didn't know the first thing about. But I put my heart into it - Day in and day out I put in effort - pushed by my superstition. 

Together with this IFS mains preparation, I had to deal with a lot of personal problems too but everyone will have their fair share (so, irrelevant). 

But I didn't do great at the exam (even after multiple revisions and all) because of lack of sleep on the previous nights of the exam and health issues. I managed to complete every paper though. 

I highly suspected if I'd get an interview call - but my superstition told me that there is a chance because not everyone prepares five months for this exam. And I did get an interview call. My hopes went sky high once again.  So this was my first IFS interview and my last IFS attempt. Again, the interview was 5 months away. 

So I got married and started our independent life in between. For some time I put preparations away. When the interview schedule was out - mine was on the first day. Once again I fell into full on preparation mode - determined not to botch it for a second time. By the interview date, I was confident enough.
However, my IFS Personality Test was very lackluster - no interesting conversations, so many 'I don't know' responses - I felt very disappointed afterwards. The long wait began as the interview schedule was there for another 20 days. 

The results were expected on Wednesday (28th June) or latest by Friday (30th June). But since it was not released on both these days - I expected it only on Monday (3rd July). So I decided to go for a movie.

I got inside the movie theater with my life partner and one minute before the movie started the results were out (I forgot to turn my internet off). And I searched for my name - first four letters showed one result and since I had a relatively rare name my heart throbbed - but the fifth letter typed in brought the results to 0 - telling me that my name is not so rare after all. On the screen the villain was thrashing a dog to death - how metaphoric! 

I haven't felt despair like this in my life. I wanted to run out of the movie hall but I sat there till the end. I cried a lot afterwards. I want to go back in time and change things. Celebrations had started in people's statuses and groups. But 10 years of my life went poof! 

People tell me I'll do good in life. But I really don't know how. With such a long career gap, no skills added and such high ambitions.. I really feel I have proved all those who asked me to quit this uncertain journey. I felt the need to jot this down because I see an ocean of aspirants pouring in every year. I know we will never see it when we are in it. But when reality hits, it's very hard. 

Some of these might feel very childish to at least a few of those reading this. But nevertheless I felt I should tell my story even though it's not a success story. I imagined this write-up very differently. I wish I could write a happy ending - reaching a much larger audience. But there is no happy ending now. So I will leave this incomplete...

Disclaimer: NOT EVERYTIME SUCCESS STORIES TO BE SHARED. Sharing it for larger interest and a silent message that DON'T OVERDEPEND ON THIS UNPREDICTABLE PSC ! Keep your backups ready and don't wait too much for all the important decisions of your life on this single exam !! #Sharing_is_Caring 😢😐🙏

docs.t:
Name - Ritwik Mehta
Date - 11/05/23 (Afternoon) 3rd to go
Board- Smita Nagraj Ma’am
Optional- Geography 
College- Kirori Mal College, DU [BA Hons Geography]
Profession (if any) - Not mentioned in DAF
Hobbies - Nothing asked (Blogging, Cricket, English comedy movies)
Achievement - Remote Sensing essay (among others) - 1 question

Interview started at 3.05. Entered and wished good afternoon. Ma’am asked me to take a seat and asked me whether I had joined police services somewhere? I said “No ma’am” and she laughed and said - “I’m asking because you were standing in attention with your thumbs pointing down.” I said - “No ma’am, again” and laughed. I thought that the interview would be like a conversation from here but boy was I wrong!

Smita Nagraj Ma'am:

1. What is Subaltern History? [Me, a geography student] - I was smiling but was very concerned that she has read my Optional wrong. But since I knew it well, I replied.
2. So, you come from Jharkhand. Now, if we have to present a subaltern view of what the local inhabitants of Jharkhand, the tribals experience in today’s world. What would such an account be? [Me - :O] - Started by saying there is some improvement - but she cut me short and said -
3. No. Forget that. Not our view of development. Their perspective on what has happened? [By this time, I had got time to think so I answered this pretty well pointing out challenges in their lived experience but ending on a hopeful note that even tribals groups would appreciate the benefits of political representation, FRA and development after centuries of exploitation. Also, I added a few “geographical hooks”, aiming to take the conversation away from this. Thankfully ma’am took this.]
4. Ok. I noticed you mentioned Trickle down. So tell me is this theory and what are the limitations to it. Also, what are the issues with collection of kendu leaves? [Explained trickle down and added more geographical pointers with concepts like Growth Pole, Myrdal etc. She stopped me after a point and said -]
5. But do you really think trickle down is still an viable developmental model seeing how it has been challenged? [Responded with balanced view that while we have to also shift to bottom up, participatory models of growth - trickle down still makes economic sense - couldve added some discussion from Economic Surveys on this but didnt reach there]
6. Ok so back to my question. Kendu leave collection issues? [Didnt really know the issues with collection but gave a few points of marketing infra missing, over reliance on forest department and middle men. I was not satisfied with this answer but I really couldnt think more at that point.]

She said Ok. Thats it from me. [Said thank you ma’am.] So far so good. The whole subaltern thing came a bit out of the blue but I was feeling good. After this, it was pure carnage. It seemed like Chaube sir’s board had transported into the room.

M1 [sitting directly to my right - was a bit grumpy and in grilling mode. Visibly bored]

1. What is parallel cinema? [Sorry sir, dont know] - Couldve asked for taking a guess but decided against it.
2. What is meaningful cinema? [Sorry sir, dont know]
3. Dont you have any interest in cinema? [Yes sir I do but I havent heard these terms before.]
4. What is the difference between storm, cyclone, and hurricane? [Me again confused because storm is a generic term and the only difference is of intensity with respect to cyclone. While cyclone and hurricane are different only in nomenclature. However I gave this same reply but it became long winded and resulted in some back and forth :(]
5. How are cyclones named? [Answered]
6. Earlier, cyclones had feminine names. Why? [Said dont know but asked for a guess. And here is where everything can get potentially dangerous for me. I guessed that maybe some misogynistic view of destruction being associated with women could be to blame. And as I said this, I saw M4 looking to the Chiarperson with a large smile. This threw me off completely and I thought I messed up.]
7. But, even if you look at Greek mythology, women have been associated with creation and life? [Took this opportunity to clarify that yes sir I am unaware and maybe my guess is completely wrong. I will have to learn more on this. Thank you.]
8. What is NCPCR? [Answered]
9. What do you understand by child rights? [Answered generically]
10. What is the law for protecting children from sexual offences? [Answered but fumbled with the POCSO Act]
11. What is right to defamation and right to damages? [I knew defamation, I knew right to damages but “right to defamation” stumped me. I didnt have the courage to say that sir I dont think there is any “right” to defamation so I simply said I dont know and left it at that.]

By this point, I’ve said I dont know thrice and potentially messed up on a question. So when he pointed to the next panel member, I couldnt say Thank You and turn away fast enough. :P

M2 [sitting to my left - seemed like someone with Defence, IR specialization. Neutral demeanour - calmer than M1]

1. What are the technologies needed in Remote Sensing? [Answered]
2. What is weapons diplomacy? [I asked to take a guess and answered this well enough. Included India’s approach in neighbourhood and US Washington Declaration.]
3. Ok so we hear about North Korea conducting these large tests. Even recently it did one. So how does it get the technology and funding for it? [Me = :O - How am I supposed to know North Korean funding. But i responded with internal economy + potentially gets help from China, Russia. Could’ve included some aspect on proliferation from Pakistan, weapons trade etc but didnt remember in the moment.]
4. Is North Korea really a threat if it has these weapons? [Responded with it not being a responsible state actor, sparking arms race etc.]
5. What is the National Security Council’s composition? [Didnt remember the composition so I only said it is headed by NSA and outlined its functions.]
6. What are three factors of rural development? [Answered]

He said thats it from me and passed on to M3.

M3 [sitting to the Chairperson’s right - neutral demeanour but random questions]

1. India’s rank is 132nd on HDI. What is HDI and how do we improve it? [This had so much content potential that I had to stop myself from speaking after a point as he seemed bored.]
2. Has NEP been able to target these interventions you talked about in improving education? [Gave a generic response]
3. What are Intellectual Property Rights? [Answered]
4. Ok so Russia Ukraine was has been going on. Now India has abstained from voting against Russia. So can you tell the historical basis for India’s abstentions? [I started giving reasons about strategic autonomy and India’s view that this is Europe’s war]
5. He heard some and then said yes but what is the historical basis for not voting agains Russia. [I apologized and replied with historical ties, Russia standing up for India in UNSC and defence and diplomatic support etc.]
6. President Zelensky has given a 10 point peace plan. Do you feel this can end the conflict? [Said I dont know what this plan is.]
7. Ok China has also given a plan. Can that bring peace? [Dont know China’s solution either -_-]
8. Can India help in bringing peace? [Answered this well.]
9. What is the state of forest in India as per the latest report? [Answered well with data]
10. Which states are underperforming? [Said dont know exactly which states :( ] 
11. What is Intanglible Cultural Heritage? [Answered]
12. Is there any ICH from Jharkhand? [Thanked Vision ka prelims mocks of the past 4 years lol - said Chhau dance and relaxed a bit]

He passed on to M4 and I was glad this was over. I looked to M4 who was smiling and I realized that I too have to smile xD. So that happened.
M4 [sitting to the Chairperson’s left - pleasant and cordial.]

1. Continuing from ISFR, who prepares this report? [Answered]
2. What technologies are used? [thankfully remembered the satellite used and added generic terms like sensors, GPS, ground truthing data etc]
3. So we started our Nuclear program years ago and yet - Ok tell me what is the status of Nuclear in India? [That morning, Indian Express editorial had the number - 6780 MW which has stuck with me. I said this figure and he smiled and said stop stop you know. So, continuing - ]
4. So what are the challenges? Why are we not able to expand nuclear? [Answered with raw materials, civil nuclear liability issues, environmental concerns etc.]
5. What is the performance of Ayushman Bharat? What challenges is it facing? [Really couldnt remember a lot. Said onboarding of hospitals as an issue but beyond that I havent looked into performance]

He said thats it from me. I looked over at the Chairperson and she said - “Ok that is it, Thank you.” Thanked them and came out. 

Total time - 28 mins approx.

Overall experience - Cant say as the interview was not really as conversational or cordial as I had been expecting. Almost nothing came from the prepared list of hundreds of questions I went with except maybe ISFR, Nuclear, Rural Development and Remote Sensing. Nothing repeated from mocks other than one different question on Nuclear. Initially I felt it was terrible but as time is passing, I feel it was more or less fine. Not very different from what I was doing in mocks. Also, the 2 members sitting directly to your right and left makes it very awkward and eye contact is very unnatural xD

PS - Just kidding but whoever had put parallel cinema as their hobby did me a great disservice lol. Next time se sab log apne hobbies PT verified group pe daal dena taki baki log bhi prepare kar le ye sb -_-. Mera cricket pe kiya hua 4 month PhD, useless ho gya. 

Utility of mocks or O2O (if any) -  Took around 10-12 mocks as this was my first interview and I had too much time. However, apart from the ability to withstand the urge to make multiple guesses, I dont think there was any tangible bearing on the final interview. But this couldve been very different had questions in the interview been different. O2O with Khan sir was the highlight for me but apart from this, NACS, Chahal, Vajiram, Raus, and Vajiro were good.
