Interview almost entirely from the DAF. Was really scared of getting Soni sir’s board and eventually that is where I ended up. Can’t analyse how the interview went, everyone’s face was poker, a few members grilled. Chairman scolded me over mismatch of face and photo since I had shaved. Interview started on a very depressing note. I kept smiling and confident for the rest of the interview, nonetheless. 
Chairman sir-
1. What does your name mean? (It means Silver) Follow ups- What are some uses of silver? Where is it found in India? Is it found naturally?
2. Do you watch television? If you find any immoral or objectionable content on TV, where will you report? 
3. Which Geographic characteristics of India help it in economic growth? (Apart from the location, monsoon, resources, I also mentioned about population as an asset), light grilling on this part. Is population an asset or an obstacle? (I mentioned skilling, demographic dividend and China’s success story)
Member 1-
4. You have unique hobbies. What does aquascaping mean? (Landscaping inside an aquarium to make it resemble an actual biotope) Do you practice it commercially? How many aquariums do you have?
5. Which landscapes have you created in these aquariums? I said East Asian (Mekong), South American (Amazon) and African (Lake Malawi)
6. Do you also keep Piranhas? Why not? What are the issues? Where do you get these exotic fish in India?
7. About this Mekong, where does it begin and end? 
8. Your other hobby- Backpacking. What is it, where did you travel last? (Badrinath-Valley of Flowers and most recent stay-cation at Manali).
9. Let’s talk about Manali. Where did you stay, where did you sightsee? (Stayed in a hostel for 15 days and studied, only went for treks, no sightseeing). Where are these treks? Temperature there? Snow? (I was there for the first half of march)
10. Which river in Manali? Its geographic characteristics? Which other river? (Beas and Manalsu)
11. Who was Vyas? (I said maharshi Vyas, the author of Mahabharata) Something else about Vyas? Philosophy? I said sorry.
Member 2-
12. You belong to Amravati. Which part of Mahrashtra is it in? (Vidarbha). Which part covers Marathwada?
13. What is with the separate state demand for Vidarbha? (Reasons- Disparity, underresresentation, etc) (I said it has phased out due to increased attention and development in Vidarbha)
14. Is Nagpur comparable with Pune, development wise? When will it be comparable?
15. Which are the resources in Vidarbha? What is MahaGenCo? Which are the thermal power plants around Nagpur? How far are these? Do they lead to pollution? What should we do? (Koradi and Khaparkheda, earlier much outside Nagpur’s borders, now Nagpur has grown. We shouldn’t shun these industries instantly but aim for CCS and gradual shift to renewables).
Member 3-
16. Let’s talk about Amravati. Has Amravati given any President to the country? (I heard precedent and gave some other answer, she corrected me). 
17. Which big industrial projects will help Amravati. Asked about a railway project.
18. Why does Taiwan have claims on South China sea even though it is far from there? (I mentioned UNCLOS and EEZ and right to exploration)
19. China and Taiwan have issues. Who claims what? She added, Taiwan claims that China belongs to Taiwan and that’s why it claims South China sea.
20. You are a Project Executive of water supply scheme in a block. There severe shortage of funds due to non-payment of dues by the people. Scheme is difficult to be managed without finances. What will you do? (I focussed on cpntinuity in water supply apart from recovering the dues legally. Getting finances through other legal channels. (She was expecting a focus on community participatory approach in convincing the defaulters).
Member 4-
21. You are from Fergusson. Did you see these NDA aspirants? (Had no clue)
22. Who is Barack Obama? Why famous? (First African-American President of the USA.) Which African country did he belong to? 
23. There is some other Barak in India. A river. Where? (Mistakenly said it originates in Assam, he grilled over it on how can a geography specialist get this wrong). What is its specialty? (Most species of fish in a single river-2000. Didn’t know.)
24. There are river dolphins. Where are they found in India?
25. Difference between Gangetic Dolphin and Indus Dolphin? Where is Indus Dolphin found in India? (Beyond Harike in Beas, extinct in India).
26. You are newly posted as an SDM in a town. The local MLA invites you over tea as a courtesy call. Will you go or will you ask him to come to you? (I said I won’t go and I.ll politely say I would ask him to meet when the formal occasion so demands). He said politicians may hold grudge against you and not cooperate in future. I said I’ll not go at loggerheads with him but gently inform him that we’ll meet when the occasion so demands.
27. Should compulsory military service for youth be followed in India? (I said we have a large population unlike countries such as Israel where this is done. We can make military like training in schools mandatory to imbibe discipline, but not force people to serve the military).
Chairman sir- We are done, you may go.
Spent the next 2 hours proving to the officials of UPSC that I am the person in the photo. 
Recommendations on mocks- will give it if I get good enough marks to back that recommendation up.

sir asked how would india with its credentials of peace can bring about an end to this conflict.. we have seen sri sri ravishankar.. sadhguru who are doing lot of good work.. how can this message of peace be worked upon

sir the changes suggested in the 2015 amendment act was good enough but that dint go through.. the changes i would like to bring in sir is..
for the projects involving national interest like rural infrastructure, defence corridors, industrial corridors, if we can remove difficult procedures like social impact assessment and taking the consent of everyone.. it will be easier for acquiring land for national purposes...

sir then passed on to last old member (male) who was quite cheerful..
sir asked since u have done computer science engineering.. and there is 2g, 3g, 4g, 5g, 6g.. among 2g and 3g which is better for india... 
i said sir.. since 2g is less speed and more latency and 3g is more speed and less latency i would say 3g is better

sir said - 2g is indigenous technology.. 3g we have to import.. isn’t 2g better in that perspective..
i said sir except for the national security reasons like borrowing technology from china, 3g,4g or 5g is better suited as they are the modern technologies which people prefer.. coming to indigenous technology our honourable prime minister has launched 6g test bed and 6g in future is going to be an indigenous technology...
sir repeated so 6g is going to be indigenous in future.. i said yes sir..

then manoj soni sir took over and said the usual lines with a slight smile

docs.k: Indore, Biology, Chess, American music
docs.t:
Manoj Soni Sir
DAF Keywords- Indore, Biology, Chess, American music
Duration- 25 minutes, first to go. Started after 2.15 pm in afternoon shift, much later than other boards. 

Opening thoughts- grand chambers of the chairman. Beautiful round table. Smiling Soni sir asked to be seated, removed mask so he can verify the picture. Said it was my choice to wear or not wear the mask. 

C: How are you feeling today?
- Read out DAF and said you have a variety of interests, studied from eminent institutions etc. How did you get interested in your graduation subject
- You are from MP, so you must be well prepared with the cheetah reintroduction, so I am not going to ask anything from there *everyone laughs*.
- Have you heard of a prestigious research institute in hyderabad?
- Have you visited CCMB? Did you ever think of pursuing PhD from there?
- Do you understand Sanskrit? Can you recite the full shloka of which Vasudhaiv Kutumbakam is a the ending phrase of?
 - goes on to recite it himself, as I said I dont know.
- What is the meaning of VK and do you think this is a practical idea today? Discussed about India's leadership on this front. 

M1 (straight forward questions, few counters but no grilling)
- Are you aware about crypto? Can it be regulated? Discussion followed.
- What about drones? What are their applications?
Cannot recall some questions. 

M2 
- Since you like American music, have you heard of Bob Dylan? What do you think about him getting a Nobel?
- You have played chess. Tell me, if I keep one grain of wheat on one square, 2 grains on 2nd square and so on, what quantity of wheat is required to fill up 64 squares?
- Indore has been the cleanest for long now. How has this behavioural change been cultivated in people?
- How can you apply the same to Delhi dumps? Smiled and said, good, I think you will clean Delhi as well. 

M3 (spoke very slowly, fortunately was sitting very close. Cordial member)
- Continuing with chess, what is the difference in approach between chess and *some Chinese board game* that I hadn't heard of. 
- What can be the implications of trans national animal habitats? 
- What security threats are posed by translocation of animals? How can this be managed?

M4 (longest interaction, almost 10 minutes)
- Are you aware of *some south african animal corridor*? Said no
- What is the utility of animal corridors
- What is the difference in animal corridors built in India and in other countries? 
- Are you interested in international relations? I unknowingly did a very enthusiastic nod. 
- What do you think about the Russia Ukraine war? 
- Do you see any correlation between war and defence manufacturing companies?
- What does your company do? (DAF)
- What is your role? Tell us what all steps you follow once you receive a manuscript? How many hours you give?
- What is minimum wage? Discussion followed. 

C: Your interview is over. Take very good care of yourself. 

Mocks- 7-8 mocks. Board was not overly cordial or smiling throughout, but there was no grilling and minimum cross questions even in questions that were followed by a longish discussion. Nothing extraordinary or life changing, just another day at office.

M2 (he maintained a poker face throughout with an ocassional smile): 
1. Why is there so much superstition in our society? 
2. Long monologue on scientific temper and rationality. Has our state been unable to foster scientific temper in our society? 
3. Long monologue on man animal conflict with multiple questions: why it happens? Should humans take precedence over animals? To what extent it should be allowed? How do we manage long term? (I ended my answer saying the long term way ahead is to sensitize communities for peaceful coexistence and the member seemed to agree) 
4. Asked if I could give an example of peaceful coexistence of humans and animals. (Could not recall at the moment and he gave a brief description of Gir forest) 

M3 (very pleasant): 
1. Difference between religion and superstition? 
2. What would did you do at NITI Aayog (I described my work which also involved work on Global Hunger Index)

4. Does it highlight a failure of policymaking? How can we improve ourselves? 
5. difference between planning commission and NITI.

M4 (looked pretty serious throughout): 
1. I had mentioned about a data governance project that I was part of at NITI, so asked me about few data sources of the Government. 
2. Which ministry published NHFS? 
3. Any other organisation that helps in data collection of NFHS? 

He asked one more long question that I can't recall now. But to this question, the chairman interrupted and said "In essence, this is what he means....." and reframed the question precisely. 

M5 (very serious): 
1. Why has Dharavi been in the news recently? (College and previous work in Mumbai for 7 years)
2. List out 5 salient features of Dharavi. 
3. What made covid management in Dharavi so efficient?

Chairman :  (Full of Positive Energy)
Asked me to sit. Offered Tea or Coffee. I politely refused as I already drank outside I told.
1. So You read Non-Fictional Books. Which are the awards given at national and International Level for Books ?

2. Interrupted Me and Asked,What are the categories under Booker Prize ?
Sorry Sir I don't know.
3. Tell some other Awards ?
At National Level Sahitya Akadami and At State Level given by state governments for local language promotion.
4. What are the names of state level awards ?
In Rajasthan it is rajasthani sahitya akadami but I don't know exact name in other states Sir.
5. Tell Some Private Sector Awards ?
Sir Media Foundations like The Hindu and Indianexpress give but I don't know exact names.
6. What Does This year's Economic Survey says about the status of indian economy ?
I was about to answer it in general terms but luckily I remembered that Since It is interim budget year, Economic Survey is not presented. ( He was like yes - this is what I was looking for and gave the turn to other member to ask questions )

Member 1 : ( Below 3rd and 4th Question were quite unclear)
1. How can Ethical and  Hacking go together when Hacking itself is illegal ?
I told sir under IT Act,2000 hacking is illegal but that is due to unauthorized access and In Ethical Hacking the person is hired by organizations to scan vulnerabilities in system so he is duly authorized to do so. It is formally Called ' Penetration Testing' within IT Sector.
2. What do you mean by ethical hacking - Data Security or network security or both ?
Answered it is both.
3. How can we make a system full-proof ?
Sir Nothing can be full proof in digital domain permanently for example current strongest algorithms can be solved by Quantum computers in minutes. So we have to constantly stay ahead and keep upgrading security of digital infrastructure. 
4. How to make a system secure from hacking ? 
Sir It depends on objectives and usage of the digital system as well as the cost available with us to provide cybersecurity and sensitiveness of the data being transferred.
5. So you play badminton regularly  ?
On weekends when exam is more than one month away but if less than one month to exam I shift to other hobbies.
6. Tell me why badminton is becoming so popular ?
Recent success of players and good network of academies of former champions, adapting to indian conditions just like street cricket now being played street badminton too, government support to players and emphasis on creation of infrastructure motivates players too.

Member 2 : (Quite Disinterested Face)
1. So you are from electronics background, tell me how does LLM ( Generative AI Model) integrate with Quantum Computing and how can that be used to tackle climate change ?
Sorry Sir, I don't know exact integration of LLM with Quantum Computing
2. So You have background in ethical hacking and drone making, you must have read about drones in detail ?
I clarified that these were just one day workshops but since drones have become such important part of our socio-economic environment,I have studied about them.
3. In a Drone,which is more important payload or structure  ?
( I asked for clarification)
I told sir it depends upon the usage of drone - for example if it is being used in defence or e-commerce delivery then payload is more important but In surveillance, intelligence gathering,ISR Operations - structure becomes important.
He told that Payload is more important as it  has sensors but anyways moving on.(I felt he was wrong as sensors has nothing to do with payload but are considered part of drone structure but I replied Thank You for informing me Sir)

4. Tell me difference between Drone Deterrance and Drone Dissuation ? 
Sorry Sir I don't know , I will read about it.

I replied that Sir Bank Merger were initiated.... he interrupted me

5. What model of bank ownership shall we follow in india - private or public sector ?

Recently destination wedding concept getting popular and when high profile people visit here - gives more popularity in social media- attracts more tourists.

Sir Any state is dependent on people and it cannot survive without them working in tandem with it and when these states were increasingly surrounded by british and they started controlling people,economy,polity and nearby states, these states made treaties with them.

Sir I am not sure but I think he won Raman Magsaysay in 2014.
6. Why is he called Waterman ?
Because He makes the areas water surplus from water scarce or water deficit.

Situation Where we recharge more water than what we extract. For example - 100 litres a city is extracting from groundwater then it must recharge more than this amount.

With help of traditional water harvesting systems for recharge and with help of panchayat he removes obstruction from river path by Consensus building.

Your experience in interview- board was extremely cordial. Initially when I entered there were 4 members, another ma'am joined in the middle of the interview. Interview was 70% from DAF.
Ma'am wished good morning, I wished the others as well. She read out the DAF loudly.
CP:
1. You're from West Bengal or Rajasthan? Then why did you go to Rajasthan for graduation?
2. There was a common entrance test in 2014 also? (There was. It was recently extended to all Central Universities)
3. Do you still play chess (Yes ma'am with a huge smile on my face. I try to play everyday.)
4. What is rapid chess? How does it differ from classical chess?
5. What is the time control? (Classical chess sometimes has 1.5 hours time control for games. Said that). 1.5 hours for every move?
6. Green Hydrogen Mission? What are the problems you can identify as a chemist?
7. And what are the benefits of it? (Ma'am didn't seem satisfied by my answer)
8. Why are we focusing so much on it?
Passed on to member 1
M1: (Ma'am who joined later.)
1. What does the NCC do? ( Said don't know the specifics ma'am)
2. But you were in NCC no? (I wasn't. CP ma'am glared at her for a good minute after this😂)
3. Acha tell me the full form of NCC. (Mental dialogue: Are ma'am dur dur tak naata nahi hai mera NCC se)
4. You've heard of NSS? What do they do? (Sorry ma'am)
5. They were there in your university? (No. They began in the year I passed out.)
6. What was the story you wrote for which you won the prize? (Asked permission if I could narrate the story. She said tell in 3 lines. Bataya maine 3 line jitna ho saka).
7. What else did you do in the literary club? What other clubs were you a part of?
8. You play the guitar? What sort of guitar? Do you sing also? ( Said no with a wide smile)
9. So you generally accompany others? (Said mostly yes but I have also performed solo once or twice)
M3:( Sir. Maine galti se ma'am bol diya inko. Thankfully he didn't hear 😂)
1. You spoke about hydrogen mission. Why are we coming out with a plan for renewable energy?
2. Agriculture in your state is mostly rice related. What problems do you have in rice cultivation
3. Do you know of soil productivity (he said something else but the essence was the same. I said I don't know exactly but if you allow me I would like to try)
4. Gave a monologue about 3 rice crops then asked me to explain. Bataya bhai generic baate.
5. Tell me about the cheetah mission.
6. But what are the benefits of it?
7. But tigers and panthers can also do the same thing. Why are we not introducing them? (I said habitat is different for them. Plus cheetahs were there in the areas we are reintroducing them)
Said there are some more reasons. Look them up.
M3: (he was to my exact left but he was speaking so low that I couldn't hear him on 2 occasions)
1. Do you think history is biased?
2. But history is fact based. Why is it biased then? (Said sir it depends on the historian's perspective as well as the new information we unearth from time to time)
3. Do you think history is dead?
4. Why should we save our museums? (I mistakenly heard should instead of why. He corrected me. Said that they are a repository of our culture. Even my interest in history began when I visited the Indian museum in Kolkata)
Two or three more questions. All were history related.
M4: (sir)
1. I'll give a situation. You are the CEO of the municipality of a city. Industries there need skilled workers, but people of the area are not willing to let migrant workers come in. How would you balance the need of all stakeholders? Take a minute and answer. (Essence of the question was this. He spoke for nearly a minute)
2. What is the time period you're giving yourself for that? (Based on my answer)
3. How would you reskill the workers? (I had said we can reskill and upskill the informal sector workers or others in the area.)
Okay thank you.
CP ma'am:
You have IPS as your first preference? Why? Everyone chooses IAS. (Mentally high-fived myself 😂)
Okay thank you. All the best.

While leaving I mistakenly picked up the pouch of gloves which belonged to someone else. Ma'am said that's yours? I said yes. Ma'am said it's yours? again in a more surprised tone. I remembered that I hadn't brought the pouch in. Said no ma'am so sorry with a smile. She also smiled.
Utility of mocks or O2O (if any): Chahal was closest to interview. But even then the questioning style was completely different. Also gave KSG and Vajirao.
O2O: Utkarsh sir from SOMP, Ravindran sir, Khan sir.
Mocks helped to fine-tune my answering style. Baaki suno sabki, karo apni.

Utility of mocks:
Don't take them seriously (EASIER SAID THAN DONE). Just look at the overall feedback and areas to improve. I gave a hell lot of mocks, some were decent, some were horrible and some very factual. This interview at UPSC was very relaxed. Luckily I wasn't asked any difficult sociology/GS/graduation questions or any random current affairs question. In fact, I prepared so much for Uttarakhand that I can clear UKPCS now! 😅 But they didn't ask anything from Uttarakhand. That doesn't mean we should not prepare, it's just that you've to be ready for everything. I was told that teaching, NCC, blood donation are very generic things and they won't ask. But you can see so many questions were asked. So don't leave any part of DAF. 

All the best! See you in LBSNAA.

Your experience in interview : It was very different from the mock interviews. Surprisingly, no questions were asked from International relations or current affairs. Very few technical questions. The board was more interested in asking personal questions (for instance, chairman sir asked about my friends circle & what qualities do my friends have etc). 

There was a lot of discussion on my hobbies & how I developed interest in them.

Some questions were very very factual (& random) like — when did the first meeting of constituent assembly take place?, tell us about the third battle of Panipat?, name the architect who constructed India Gate..etc

Conclusion : Although on unexpected lines but it was a pleasant experience.

Utility of mocks (if any) : I had given 6 mock interviews ; 4 offline — at KSG, IAS Gurukul, Rau’s IAS, Samkalp & 2 online — Byju’s & Samkalp. Utility of Mocks : I felt mocks quite enriching given one has the aptitude for knowledge and self development. I felt mocks nurture one's personality and hones them as per the need.
 
Few words for fellow aspirants based on my Experience: 
 1. It's better to enter UPSC Bhavan as early as possible without waiting to enter a bit late after the queue is shortened. 
Reason being I was rushed in to the interview very fast without getting proper time even to check whether my hairs are properly groomed or not.
 
 2. For Chaubey Sir's Board : 
a. The Chairman sits a bit farther as compared to mock arrangements . Therefore, appropriate voice modulation might be needed. 
b. Frequent head movement for eye to eye contact with all members might be difficult as the table is semi elliptical requiring full turn of head.
 
 3. UPSC Interview vs Mocks 
There is a difference in type of question asked in UPSC interview and mocks. 
In Mocks : " Why X State is Backward ?" : Relatively easy to answer. 
In Interview : " Is X State Backward ? " : This is a difficult question to answer in interview scenario. 
I felt the same for other questions too. What they want is to elicit your humble opinion ( which will include reasons as well ) 
I felt UPSC questions are a notch higher than mocks.

 
Entering the UPSC Bhavan for the First Time reminded me of the Dialogue of Chanakya Serial , "Samrat , Bharat ki Bhumi Chandan hai. Iss Mitti ko mathe par laga loge toh Har Bhartiya aapko apne hriday ka samrat bana dega" 
I put some Chandan ( Soil of UPSC Bhavan) on my forehead and proceeded. This increased my confidence, conviction and motivation many folds. It stayed till I emerged out of the Bhavan. 
 
Thank You. 
Wishing you all a very fruitful interview. Prayers to Almighty to fulfill all your wishes. 
May the forces be with you all. 
Jai Hind.

( I had not read about this act properly. So couldn't answer it with proper legal points. So gave a made up answer that govt and judiciary should develope institutional mechanism to prevent misuse of data and prevent unnecessary criminalisation of people. Again english was not so fluent) 

M3: Sir

1. What is meaning of your name Ashutosh?

( I roughly knew it was shiv purana. But I was a bit scared of taking anymore guess after being reprimanded by chairman. So simply said Sir I am not aware of it. Sir said it was shiv purana. I said ok sir)

3. Now listen carefully. My chair had asked you whether you joining civil services will be a gain for civil services or loss for electrical engineering. Answer me carefully.

(This time I decided to take a decisive stand now. And specially in question which involves choices between 2 options. I  just answered that gain for civil services)

4. How is it a gain. You will hardly ever apply your electrical engineering knowledge as DM. You will be busy in administrative tasks.
( I replied him by an example that many remote villages lack electricity and how microgrids can be a solution in that. I explained how as DM I can support seeing up of microgrids etc. Sir Did'nt say anything to my answer. Simply passed me to next member.

In between Chairman sir went out of the room for a 30-40 seconds. I had a vague feeling that this is just to see my situational response. So I simply focussed on answering question of M3 sir and Did'nt get waivered by Chairman sir going out and coming in. )

M4 sir

1. You do Sun Salutation.  Is it Surya namaskar. Why you used word Salutation. (Before I could answer question.) Ok anyways, how many steps are there in Surya namaskar?

( I told him First I do 30 surya namskar and then meditation. 

He said 15 before and 15 afterwards. I said no sir, First I do 30 surya namaskar at stretch and then meditation.)
3. In ashtang yoga, dhyaana comes before meditation or after that?

4. Awadh region is about Ayodhya and all. Why is Shaam- e- Awadh famous? 

(Told him about cultural dances, music that used to be organized in evenings since Nawabs times)

5. Ok. Why is Subah-e-Banaras famous?

(Told him about spiritual activities , prayers done in morning in Varanasi since times immemorial).

Finally Chairman Sir: It was nice talking to you. Stay safe in Delhi these days. Afterwards he said something which I couldn't understand.

Simply got up. Said thanks to all and then walked out.

Overall the atmosphere was quite nice. Even while asking me not to take guess, Chairman sir only pointed this out in a very calm and composed manner. The voice tone was still pleasant. All members gave adequate time for me to reply. 2 answers I did not know. For 2 , I couldn't frame it in nice and fluent English.

Chairman sir's room ambience is nice. For those in afternoon session, cakes, coffee, juice, water etc is there in waiting area. 

One small thing: The gloves that are provided have white type of some dust on it, which may make black suit dirty. I feel that if we have a white handkerchief then it can be used to wipe off dust gently from gloves. I rubbed my gloves in a nearby newspaper and gloves became a bit dirty. So use white handkerchief.

docs.t:
Date – 12 May 2022, Forenoon 
Board – Dr. T.C.A. Anant Sir 
Optional – Medical Science 
College – Government Medical College, Kota 
Profession – I worked as Senior Lecturer first and then as Junior Resident Doctor 
Hobbies and extra curriculars – Badminton, Trekking, Wilderness camping, Trekking, Gardening, Photography, Editor of college journal, Secretary at Avekshaa (NGO) 
My experience in interview – Very cordial board, interview was totally off beat, unlike mocks! I came out of the room satisfied with my performance. 
Utility of mocks – Guide to dressing etiquette, how to avoid falling into trap of controversies. Just one bit of my personal advice, please do not let anyone bring your morale down! I gave 6 mocks, 4 went fantastic, 1 was not so good and one went horrible, the chairperson of that board ended up calling me arrogant and my confidence and morale went lower then the stock market. But then I talked to a very senior IAS officer 2 days back and he said “Beta tum waha Naukri maangane nai ja rahe ho k sir mai berojgar hu mujhe naukri pe rakhlo, unko tumhari zarurat h ye desh chalaane k liye, iss confidence k sath jao tumhara interview bahut acha jayega.” And I got the much needed booster dose against the disease that infests aspirants right at this crucial moment. 
Questions asked –  
Chairman – (he was eating a samosa at this moment) 
1. So__, you graduated in 2018 ( I corrected him and said I graduated in 2019 because 1 year is compulsory internship), he said no further in this matter. 
2. So why is it that young bright minds like you are leaving the medical profession and coming for civil services? Recently Honourable Health Minister presented data to parliament that there is shortage of doctors? (He was factually wrong at this as the HM had said that there is one doctor for 832 population, more than WHO norm of 1:1000 but I didn’t want to correct him at this moment because in that mock which went horrible was because of this fact itself and they took offence)  
3. Ok. So you like wilderness camping? Tell me about it. (I shared my experience from my last camp) 
4. When was this? Where did you camp before this? ( It was Dras) 
5. Which group did you camp with? (I said that sir I didn’t go with any group, we were three friends) 
6. So what camping gear do you use and how will you guide me if I wanted to go for a wilderness camp?  
Member 1 
7. So you’re a doctor. Are you aware of EUA, Emergency Use Authorisation and the normal process? ( I didn’t know about the normal process and I said sorry) 
8. What are the ethical concerns in clinical trials and why is India the soft target for these trials? 
9. What is the difference between NCEs and generics? 
10. Can biologics be patented? ( I said yes but he double questioned, are you sure? I hope I’m right that biologics can also be patented) 
Member 2 –  
11. So during pandemic you must have seen the reverse migration. What do you think is this issue? Why weren’t we able to provide for migrants? (I fumbled here a bit and concluded by saying that administration should have taken a greater proactive approach) 
12. Has the government done anything for migrants? (At this time the caffeine from Honourable Chairperson hit him and he got up using the toilet and I also stood up and ended up losing my concentration to the answer, sat back down and answered about all the initiatives) 
13. There is lot of malnutrition in India. What are the precise statistics? What has the government done and what should be done according to you? 
Member 3 (Lady) –  
14. We have already talked about your interests. Now I want to talk about my interests. Can you name the mangroves of India? (I was only able to recall 3) 
15. Name some bird sanctuaries of India, especially from Rajasthan. (my home state is Rajasthan, again I named only 3) 
16. What is Project Tiger? (I don’t think I gave a satisfactory answer to this as I was not able to recall the exact figures but I did talk about its success) 
17. So if you’re posted as DM of one of the district with rich wildlife areas, what will be your
focus? ( I talked about my personal experiences from trekking and she seemed to be very convinced) 
18.  So _, what do you think about the elderlies? Are we doing enough for them? (By this time she didn’t know the focus are of my NGO was elderly care and was amused to know the same and I shared my personal experiences and concluded by saying that we should not look upon a 65 yr old as a dependant and use the knowledge, experience and wisdom of these people in nation building, for instance, providing vocational education to childen as has been envisaged in NEP 2020) 
Member 4 – (this gentleman wanted me to be Alexander the great and to conquer all the neighbouring counties for India) 
19. What is your take on Russia – Ukraine war? Who is to blame? ( I blamed Russia as well as NATO, NATO for expanding eastwards and wanting to bring under their umbrella, Ukraine and Georgia) 
20. So by this virtue, India should invade Nepal because it is favouring China? (I said we need to diplomatically engage and resolve issues) 
21. But if China invades Nepal, should we not invade Nepal? ( I said if that is the case that Nepal has already been invaded then Nepal’s political leader would want to align with India and we should jointly do the needful) 
22. Tell about Siliguri corridor? 
23. Isn’t it a strategic challenge for India? 
24. To secure connectivity between mainland India and NER, should we not invade Bhutan and Nepal and adjacent areas of Bangladesh to remove the issue altogether? (I said rather than coercive action and bringing them in India’s sovereign jurisdiction, we should bring them under our economic sphere, develop inland waterways, cross border road connectivity and capitalise on Kaladan project) 
25. So you don’t want to invade them. Do you believe our intelligence agencies even have any sway over these countries?  (I said we should continue intelligence gathering but respect westphalian values as well) 
26. Was Sikkim part of India in 1947?  
27. So when did India invade Sikkim? (I humbly corrected him and said Sikkim came to India out of free will and not coercion) 
28. There is something called job satisfaction. Do you think a you being a doctor will have any satisfaction by working in ministries like communication? (I agreed and said that sir share this apprehension and I have given detailed thought to it and came to a conclusion that I will always work probono, I have great regard and interest in medical profession and will always continue that and we also see that many DMs and SPs who are doctors are establisihing their OPDs when residents go on strike) 
29. Ok, thank you. 
Chairperson – Ok, thank you.

He also confirms my first name. I was then asked to take off my face mask and shield for verification. He compares my face with the photograph that I had provided and brought up some difference with regard to a scar/mole on the right side of my face which seemed prominent in the photo but absent on my face. A minute or two went by trying to find this scar until the chairman, lady member on the panel and I came to a conclusion that it might have been a temporary bruise or something.
I was told that the face mask was compulsory but the face shield was optional. Hence I attended the interview without my face shield.

Chairman: 
- So we have a poet among our midst.
(I reply 'an amateur poet sir')

- So you are in service already. IRAS. I see that you were alloted the service after the 2019 exam but joined quite late. 
 (I explain about being on Extraordinary Leave for a year and then joining training in January 2022)
- So what all parts of your training have you completed?
- Would you consider yourself as a person with a lot of inner strength, strong values? Are you a person who holds on your opinions no matter what?
- What if your superior gives you a task where you have to do something that is totally against your value system? What if you have a good understanding about this topic and feel that what the superior is saying is not the way to do things?
- What if it was a scenario where you have to draft a cabinet note? 
- What if it was completely against your values and conscience? Will you do the job or recuse yourself?
(During the course of answering one of the previous qns I mentioned about putting down my advice in writing in the file)
- So you are in Hyderabad now as part of your training. Have you visited some of the famous places there? Like Hussain Sagar, Golconda Fort, Char Minar?

- But you've been in Hyderabad for so long, since January and you haven't visited the other places?

Me: Education --> rational outlook

They on the one hand help you in giving simulator environment but on the other hand break your own confidence like RaosIAS did with me. Give 4,5,6 mocks and I think you can develop your confidence within this much feeding. 
That's all from my interview. Best of luck to all.

Overview:
I might be forgetting a couple of questions, the interview lasted around 25 minutes, but for me it felt that the interview was over in a flash.
Mock interviews are good for practice and give you an idea of topics to cover. But don't overdo them, take time to be able to implement the feedback given in mocks. The interview board was mixed, chairman mam was cordial and supportive, 2 members seemed slightly disinterested, 2 member seemed to test my patience by making me repeat things etc. Overall I felt the questions were mostly MP based and could have been more multi dimensional, but the pro was that the questions were relatively easy and relevant to my DAF. My only advice would be to stay calm and confident and believe in yourself throughout the duration of interview. One more advice, try to find atleast 5 minutes where you settle yourself before the interview, I didn't have that luxury as I was almost instantly called up after doing my document verification. All the very best!!

It has already become one of the most memorable day of my life and so would be yours. May the force be with all of us.* 

Now fingers crossed. Countdown begins for result. Notwithstanding, wherever we may fall in CSE Result,this is very beautiful journey and would always be cherished. 

Mukund.

M2 - What about transport - we have Min of Shipping, Highways etc

M2- What is spiritual quotient?

M2 - So you read self help books! Who’s your fav author and why?
A - James clear wrote Atomic Habits. Practical insights to build good habits. Told few tips when he asked..
M2 - So Stephen R Covey has wrote 7 habits of highly effective people. What are those 7 habits?
A - Listed 4 and then said not able to recall more.
M2 - You won this award. Tell me about the smokeless stove and how it works. 
A - Told about air draft mechanism, double top and a chimney - all resulting in less Indoor Air Pollution 
M2 - Do you know fracking?
A - Sir, I have heard it in context of Shale Gas. To extract shale gas trapped in rock.
M2 - Asked on shale oil and where are reserves in India.
A - Talked of ONGC recent discovery in West Bengal of Rs 50,000 cr + KG Basin + Gujarat.
M2 - What about North East?
A - Sir, in Assam, yes. 

M3 (male - He was interrupting a lot/not letting me finish (I guess as part of pressure tactics) and taking topics to a tangent from things I spoke +
seemed harsh) 
M3 - What is energy security? how is our energy security? What are we doing for that.
A - Told of 85% oil dependance and how vulnerable like Iran geo-politics
Some counter questions on whether it makes us insecure or no. He said we will buy from someone else, what’s the issue then. (I held my ground) I said yes we can, but Iranian oil is cheap, oil quality good and 60 day credit period etc. Then asked on quality of oils, sweet oil etc - I said Texas oil..and said I don't know sir. Then he moved to other question.
M3 - Which is the country that is saying visit us before we drown?
A - Sir, I can’t recall. 
Just when he was shifting the baton to M4, I said, sir Mauritius?
M3 - He smiled broadly along with M4 and said its Maldives, but yes, very close!

M4 (Lady Member) - Asked on More Crop, Per drop phrase. What is it? What are we doing for it?
A - Talked of shift to water productivity from land productivity. We are implementing PM Krishi Sinchayee Yojana, Har Khet ko Jal, Micro irrigation and partnership with Israel etc
M4- What are the technologies for saving water in agri?
A - Rain water harvesting, Drip irrigation, Drones for sensing soil/water, ISRO’s Bhuvan Satellite to map groundwater etc 
M4 - What we are doing to climate proof agriculture?
A - Talked of drought and flood resilient varieties from prestigious IARI, National Mission on Sustainable Agriculture under National Action Plan on Climate Change + agro climatic planning. 
M4 - Asked me schemes/govt steps for rural women? 
A - Told about Ujjawala Yojana, Rural Livelihood Mission, SBA. On asking more, PM MVVY, ICDS, Beti Bachao Beti Padhao.
In between she confirmed about Beti Bachao Beti Padhao and Livelihood Mission. 
A - Told of awareness, saving accounts etc in BBBP and of SHGs in Livelihood Mission
M4 - What is empowerment (I assumed asking in context of women)?
A - Empowerment means expanding the choice/freedom and capability for women- it has social, political, economic dimension.
M4 - So you know all about schemes! Tell me whether these schemes are actually empowering women.
A - (Being all positive and somewhat ) and Yes, definitely. Talked of how Ujjawal helped remove 8 crore women's drudgery to fetch firewood removed due to , toilets for women etc. 
M4 - Its good they get LPG but do you think women have freedom enough to say that we wont cook.?
A - (Tried to be all positive and gave personal touch) Ma’am, these are long held social traditions. But gender parity is coming in terms of sharing household responsibilities. We see it in urban and peri urban areas and slowly in rural areas also mindsets are changing. My own personal experience of smokeless stoves project where I saw when women got financial empowerment, they earned respect from husband. And when these women went for project even outside the state, the males were ready to pitch in for their household work. 
M4 - Nodded in agreement (as it seemed!) and looked towards CP.

CP - Okay, thank you. 
I thanked CP and other members and left. 

Overall
Was a good experience. Almost NIL questions on my graduation subject or current affairs/corona. Mostly on the DAF, optional and generic stuff. Didn’t have much issues in Mask and Shield since I was first to go, although for few seconds it becomes foggy. Happy that some luck helped in questions, answers to which I had randomly encountered - like Vladivostok example (in a youtube video), Shale in West Bengal, India Gate (from previous transcript - Thanks to this group!). Tried to back my answers with data, schemes and used key words (not jargons) from my field/hobbies/optional and maintained optimism. 

Good Luck to other candidates! Rock it.

I became very responsible and also my accountability increased as since the very first year I had to take my own decisions without asking my manager. I even learnt to take decisions in ambiguity when the requirements were not clear but still we had to move on. Also, Sir I learnt leadership skills if I may explain with an anecdote.
Hmm..
RP : Sir when I got a good rating I was sent to a Centre of Excellence team  which means that is better than even the North American Counterparts and the team members had a belief that participating in a co curricular activity is a waste of time and is done by people doing less important work. I had problems in integrating in that team and I asked my manager if we can participate in a cubicle decoration event and he told me you can do it if you want but you have to do everything yourself. It was a tough time convincing everyone but finally we did and the bond that we built was amazing and we even got prize. It was very good opportunity for me to integrate with the team.
Was the integration/bonding  because you won . would it have been the same had you lost
RP: Sir the bonding was the process of the event. We laughed, cracked jokes, came to know each other’s strengths and weaknesses. Someone was good at  cutting thermocol, someone was painting etc.
Rishu, it is often said that leaders have Tolerance to Ambiguity. What does it mean?
RP: Sir Ambiguity means something that is not clear and leaders have to take decisions even if things are not clear at the moment.
Interrupted... that is decision making in ambiguity, I am asking Tolerance to ambiguity.
RP: Sir, it means to tolerate the ambiguity and stay firm and keep working.
Ok I am done.
M1 BEGINS.
Rishu you teach underprivileged children. Who is underprivileged?
RP: Sir these are those students who not privileged to go to good schools or have supportive environment to study.....interrupted.
Good school or no school at all?

So you are an electronics engineer what was your role in the BAJA ?

What is that? You mean using sensors?
RP: Yes Sir using sensors
In this IT enabled world, what are the challenges in using IT for security?(very long question)
RP: Sir most important problem as per me is data handling as DATA is the basis of the IT enabled world so privacy is a big concern. For instance the face recognition systems.....interrupted.
How does it work?
RP: Sir, it stores the images of people in mob and then matches it......interrupted
I am asking how does it work?
RP Sir it stores the data digitally in the form of 1s and 0s (you means through marking) yes sir and then it matches them.

M2 BEGINS
You were the Editor of the Literary Society, you write short stories, How did you develop this skill?

Allowed or proposed?

M3 BEGINS: 

RPF is a specialized force and and there is another force GRP.Is there a friction between the two?

ting in. We coordinated with our seniors and staff and the 2 were arrested. I realized that better coordination can also prevent many heinous crimes.

   CM in the end looking at members. Ok your interview is over. You may  now go to your ‘Ustaads’  and get back to your training.

Shrestha Anupam, Chemical Engineer from IIT Delhi, Home state- Bihar
Board- RN Choubey Sir
Interview duration- 25-30 minutes
After I enter and greet all the members, the Chairman asks me to be seated and for the next one minute, he tries to make me as comfortable as possible by talking about pleasantries such as lunch. After he has ensured that I am comfortable and in the right zone, he starts asking the questions.
Chairman
1.  In one minute, tell me about your academic background and work experience.
-  I tell him about my schooling and graduation
2.  What is the difference b/w 2G, 3G, 4G and 5G.
-  I explain the difference in terms of data speed, bandwidth and latency.
3.  So what is it about 5G that makes it so special
-  I explain about the bandwidth, frequency, latency etc. but there is a pause when I try to recall some other points and am unable to do so. I apologise and the Chairman smiles and signals the next member to ask questions.
1st member
1.  So you have studied environment as one of the subjects in class 10th. What did you study in it
2.  What are the reasons for underdevelopment of Bihar
-  I explained about the Permanent Settlement Act. the Freight Equalisation policy, political instability after the 60s and the lack of development of industries.
3.  Is there no other reason
-  I mention the high crime rate in 80s and 90s which curbed developmental initiatives
4.  Why is there so much out-migration from Bihar?
-  I mention that Bihar has the highest population density among all Indian states (the Chairman interjects and asks me- the highest? I reply confidently, yes sir.) and the lack of industries which limit the employment opportunities which are available.
5.  What is India’s concern towards BRI and why hasn’t it joined it
-  Mentioned sovereignty and territorial integrity 
2nd member
1.  What is the meaning of your name?
2.  Aren’t they very similar? So I can call you (Shrestha)^2 or (Anupam)^2?
-  I smile and say, yes sir.
3.  What is social audit?
4.  What is Environment Impact assessment?
5.  How are our relations with our neighboring countries?
-  I replied that we enjoy amicable relations with our neighbours. He interjected and asked, “with all our neighbours “? I mentioned that there were pending issues with China and Pakistan.
6.  Do you recall any issue with China, any stand-off etc?
-  I asked for a moment to think about it and then politely enquired if he was referring to the Dokhlam stand-off. He replied in affirmative and asked me to give an account of the stand-off.
7.  Have you heard about Freudian theory?(He wanted to ask me some questions on it)
-  I replied that I had heard about it but didn’t know it in detail. He got the clue and didn’t ask me any further questions on that topic.

The Chairman signaled for the next member to take over.

3rd Member(lady member)

1.  Give me a Sociological analysis of coronavirus
-  Mentioned isolation, social anxiety, de-globalisation fears, resurgence of Indian culture(Namaste etc.)
2.  How to deal with these problems like isolation?
3.  What is the difference between a non-profit organization and a charity?
-  I asked for her permission to take a guess and then answered to the best of my understanding. She seemed at least moderately approving of what I was saying so I think I must have mentioned some correct points.
4.  Who got the Nobel Prize in Economics last year?
5.  What did they get it for?
-  Mentioned RCTs and its application
6.  Can you name another area where RCTs are used. You may take a guess if you want to. 
-  I thought for a moment but couldn’t recall. I politely told her so upon which both she as well as the Chairman told me that the other application was in drug testing.
4th member
1.  What is Indo-Pacific and what is its importance, especially to India
2.  Is our Navy equipped enough to be a Net Security Provider in the region?
3.  What are MSMEs and what is their role in the Indian economy
4.  What is constraining the MSMEs to reach their potential?
The Chairman smiles and says, “Shrestha, the ball is in your court now. Is there any area from your DAF or otherwise from where you would like us to ask you questions from or any other thing that you might want us to know about you.

I mentioned my interest in writing poetry, partly hoping that I would be told to recite a poem.(My hopes didn’t come true though :P) The Chairman asked about the topics that I write poems on. After I answer, he says, “Thank You. Your interview is over.”
 I thank all members and leave the interview room.

Overall analysis- The Board was very cordial and tried their best to make me feel as comfortable as possible. There was a visible lack of DAF-based questions and International relations was the area from where I was asked the maximum number of questions.

Brief Details:

Board: PK Joshi
Brief assessment: Extremely cordial board. I have heard negative reviews about the Board but I'd like to humbly disagree with those reviews. My experience suggests otherwise.

C: You did your schooling in Sainik School, then went to Guru Gobind Singh School, then NIT Jamshedpur and finally pursued a job in My Sigma in Bengaluru. Is that right?
S: Yes sir
C: so how often do you go to Bihar?
S: sir mostly during annual vacations.
C: so what was your job as a decision scientist?
S: sir it combines the profile of a business analyst and a data scientist. The idea is to solve business problems and take business decisions based on data rather than intuition.
C: Okay. So after 2015 you have been preparing. Where have you been living?
S: Sir I've been living in Patel Nagar in Delhi.
C: you've lived for a long time in Patel Nagar now. What are the issues in this area?
S: sir from the perspective of a student high rent is one issue. Apart from that there is an increased pressure on local infrastructure including transport infra. Also, bye laws are flouted frequently by coaching institutes and shops in the area as they run commercial operations in residential buildings.
C: okay. So if you get posted as SDM in this area how will you solve the problem?
S: Sir the first attempt would be at decongesting the area by spreading out the institutes a bit. Second, it is increasingly being realised that urban areas should actually see the coexistence of commercial and residential uses of buildings do as to reduce time spent on travel and reduce pollution. So I'd also like to tweak the bye laws a bit to accommodate that. At the same time I'll take due care that safety norms are not compromised.
C: You have studied in Sainik School. Then why did you not join armed forces?
S: Sir I have given both NDA and CDS exams. But I suffer from Eosinophilia and army does not allow entry of people suffering from it.
C: Okay. Pointed towards M2.

M2: So I see that you have lived a lot in eastern India. Born and brought up in Bihar. Then a lot in Jharkhand. Tell me why do you think there is an issue of development in eastern India while western parts like Gujarat and Maharashtra have developed well?
S: sir the reasons are multifarious. Historically while Bombay presidency did well Bihar and Odisha suffered during British rule. Second would be political where, say my state Bihar has suffered long duration of poor governance. And third would be social - caste divide continues to be deep which hampers development. When it becomes easy to garner votes based on caste identities developmental agenda takes a back seat.
M2: but these regions are resources-rich. And there are industries like Tata flourishing. Then why is the issue?
S: sir the industries in this region are capital intensive and not labour intensive. So compared to Punjab and Haryana where textile industry has generated a lot of jobs the steel industry hasn't done so in Jharkhand. An example is Jamshedpur itself. If you come to Jamshedpur you'll see a good standard of life but the same is not reflected in areas around the city. There's also the issue of what we can call quote-unquote resource curse. The region has largely been seen as one that can provide resources. The participation of tribals and their development hasn't been on agenda equally.
M2: I see you've lived a lot in Bihar and Jharkhand. Where would you say you're from?
S: Sir I'd say Bihar.
M2: okay. Tell me despite separation of Jharkhand why has it not flourished?
S: Sir Jharkhand was separated in the interest of tribal population. But the population of tribals in the state is still around 30-35% only. This has been coupled with a lot of political instability. In the first 9 years of formation Jharkhand saw 5 ch
ief ministers.

becomes difficult to grow in these conditions.
M2: okay. So you have worked in analytics. Did that involve behaviour of people?
S: yes sir. Though it's a part of overall data analytics, nonetheless it's an important one.
M2: then tell me this - using this data when an advertisement company issues a misleading advertisement on TV that you can grow tall or become slim using some product, do you think that should be banned?
S: sir actually tv advertising does not involve analytics much. The profiling is done for cases where targeting can be done. For example if you open Facebook the advertisement shown to you depends on your age, gender, location, what time of the day you are, etc. Backend profiling is done for it. In case of tv such segregation can't be done. Nonetheless, as far as misleading advertisements are concerned, they amount to cheating people directly and thus should be banned whether on TV, or social media.
M2: okay. (Nodded towards chairman)

M3 (lady): So you are from Bihar. We see there are so many good officers coming out of poor states like Bihar. And yet the state hasn't done well. What do you think is the problem? Is public service irrelevant?
S: Ma'am public service is definitely relevant as it provides institutional memory, thus helping in policy formulation and execution. However, it's not sufficient. For example in my district there is a vacancy of 52 doctors in the district hospital but only 8 doctors are working. This is because the salary given to them is Rs 44,000 only - which is not attractive for them at all. In these situations a District Magistrate becomes helpless. So whole of the government will have to be improved.
M3: Okay. There was a recent policy in Bihar on prohibition. What is the status? Has it succeeded?
S: Ma'am initially the law has done well and people's, particularly women's, response was spectacular. But lately there have been many implementation issues. First, bootlegging is becoming common, second, trafficking of both liquor and drugs has increased lately, and third in the recent raids by Bihar police in their own police stations many policemen were caught using alcohol. There have been increasing reports of women complaining that now they're losing out even more as the liquor available in black market is more costly. So no income is left with the household.
M3: And what about the impact on Scheduled castes and tribes? There is an increasing number of them in the jails?
S: yes ma'am. They were employed in the alcohol industry in large numbers and have been rendered jobless due to the ban. Due to this many have been pushed into illegal manufacture and bootlegging. We actually need to liberalise the bail norms for them. (I realize I should have also talked about jobs for them, but I didn't)
M3: but then isn't it like creating a monster first and then trying to liberalise that? We are also spending a lot on the policing to enforce it.
S: ma'am the legislation continues to be for people's welfare. And that's what the state is for. So yes there have been losses. The state has lost rs 4000 crore per annum in revenue too. But such expenses have to be taken up if welfare of people is involved.
M3: but don't you think it should be left to people to decide what they or should not do? We are in a society that is increasingly becoming educated. It should be people's choice.
S: Ma'am ideally, yes. The prohibition law is definitely like a Victorian moral legislation imposed on people. However, we need to see the social context within which the law came. The biggest stakeholders - women - came out to vote for the incumbent CM in large numbers because he had announced prohibition. They continue to be the biggest stakeholders and they support the move.
M3: but the mentality of men hasn't changed. Gender issue remains.
S: ma'am it's like looking at means and ends. If I could take another analogy to explain. If one argues that guns shouldn't be banned in US to curb violence but the reliance should solely be on social cohesion, it doesn't make sense. Both the things have to be pu
rsued in

l.
M3: big smile. Passes the buck.

M4: You have lived in Bihar, Bengaluru and now Delhi. How have you seen these places change in last 5 years? May be you have not visited Bengaluru lately. But you can talk about Bihar and Delhi.
S: Sir I'll start from Bihar. There are small to large changes. For example in my own district there was a long standing demand for a flyover as a railway gate disrupted the traffic heavily on a daily basis. Now that has been constructed by the railway ministry. There have been other infrastructural developments as well. Some cities of Bihar have progressed really well. Patna has seen large infrastructural improvements. TCS has recently opened an office in Patna. This will be helpful for students from Bihar who go out in large numbers to other states to study. Many of them want to come back but lack of jobs in IT sector hampers that. This can improve in future. Coming to Bengaluru, I have not been there recently but I do have friends there with whom I talk. Sadly I have heard more negative news about the city. There is some positive work in expansion of metro. But multiple issues have cropped up. Traffic congestion, water stress and haphazard peri-urban development are some of them. I lived in whitefield which is at one edge of the city. And already a lot of construction was taking place beyond it which was not planned well. Also, Bengaluru has one of the best weathers of the country. But slowly that is also getting compromised. Coming to Delhi, my surrounding does look the same as it was. But I can vouch for one thing. My cook has two sons. And she tells me that while earlier she was embarrassed of the fact that they studied in government school now she feels proud that they study in government schools.
M4: So you mean to say that the quality of life has gone up. Why do you think so?
S: Sir the focus on health and education by the govt has been extensive. There are the two most fundamental pillars on which quality of life is based. There are some other debatable schemes too which are populist in nature. Free water, electricity, bus rides, etc for which people should actually pay. Yet they have also helped in bringing down the cost of living for the people.
M4: Okay. You also talked about water stress. What should be done for that?
S: Sir water is increasingly becoming scarce in the country. Even a state like Bihar that has large rivers flowing through it has become water stressed. To counter this we need both local dispersed as well as large projects. Small water harvesting structures can help a lot. This can improve local resource augmentation. Take Delhi for example. It's dependent on rivers from other states. But as their own needs increase the chances of conflict for water between states will increase. So Delhi needs to augment its resources but water harvesting is yet to become common here. At the same time for large areas like Bundelkhand we need canals and dams too. We cannot make this region green only through water harvesting. Also, we will have to change lifestyle to make it less water intensive. For example in USA hand sanitizers are quite common. But rely on water for everything. Such reliance has to reduce.
M4: Okay. Passed the buck. [he had kept smiling throughout the conversation with him]

Chairman: please have seat. 
See Safin, your optional is Literature which none of us know about so we will not ask you on that. (I was like... Wow )

But I would like to ask you about some social issues if you don't mind. (Bit scary)

We can see in India, there is caste system privelent in all regions. It exists in Islam too. Can you tell us why it is there in Islam and who are these castes.

Me: Yes ma'am, there exists a caste system and hierarchy in Muslim community. For example, Syyed, Ashrafi, even my caste like Julaya. This mainly because most of the people are converted to Islam. Some because of compulsion and some because they were convinced. And because of that preexisting hierarchy, they haven't been able to incorporate the concept of equality of Islam.

Chairman: How these people have been able to sustain this system despite the concept of Equality? Why there is still discrimination?

Me: ma'am , because the Muslim upper caste has been able to reserve the right to interprete the Islamic texts. Apart from that the lower strata of community has not even able to get such education and thus have always been under the influence of the higher caste.

Chairman: you have written Julaya as your caste. This is a Weaver community right ? ( I agreed) 
Despite govt giving so much push for the textile sector and giving incentives, what we have seen is that the children of Weavers don't want to pursue the same profession. Is it the same case in Gujarat?

Me:  Yes ma'am. Even the village I come from, was once known as a Manchester of my district. But today there is noone associated with this occupation.

Chairman: Then don't you think we would be completely losing our traditional industry of handloom? What is your view on that ?

Me: Ma'am , I think, it's not about loosing the tradition but about making it more specific. For example, in Gujarat we have Bandhani and Patola which still enjoy a good status in national and international craft market. We should make efforts to promote it.

Chairman: Very good. (Passing to lady member)
M1: Safin you have this rare combination of Technology and Literature. Can you tell me who is your favourite story writer?

Me: Mr Umashankar Joshi is my favourite story writer maam. 

M1: Can you tell me about his story which you like the most ?

Me: Saap no Bharo (I made a mistake here, n said the name of his monologue drama, hope that gamble didn't come to her notice)

M1: what is it about?

Me: Maam it's about pathetic situation of daughters in our society. Story revolves around one such daughter and her mother.

M1: Though we are living in modern time, situation of women doesn't have improved much. What is the scenario in your region?

Me: Ma'am , in general what you're saying is true. But what makes me feel proud is that the village I come from has 100% female literacy and there are many couples who have only one daughter.

(Panel was impressed )

M1: Safin, do you know about online trading? Have you ever done online trading?

Me: No ma'am . But I have read about it.

M1: What are the issues concerning online trading? 
Me: Though I am not much aware about it madam ,but online trading and E-commerce  are the fields which have got prominence in today's world. It mainly suffers from online frauds where authenticity of traders and dealers is the main concern. Where there is full proof mechanism, there is no worries. But recently govt is drafting policies for the same. We hope the problems will be taken care 

M1: okay Last question. There is a govt hospital, which denies the service to woman who is in her advance stage of pregnancy as they asked for advance money which the family couldn't pay. She had to deliver the baby on nearby busstand. Though the baby and minther both are safe, some woman organizations have been demanding actions against the authorities. As a head of District,
what actions will you take?

Me: Ma'am , in this case safety and dignity of the mother and baby have been compromised. I would take strict actions against the authority as per the laws which I am yet to learn.

M1: But the hospital is denying it. They say we haven't denied.

Me: Ma'am , no woman or family will go for public delivery of baby without the compulsion. So this is primafacie a case where services have been denied.

M1: Thank you...(passing to M2)

M2: Okay. Safin. Tell me about Madressa system in our country. What has been it's contribution and how relevant are those ?

Me: Sir, there is a historically Madressa has played a great role by providing free education and other facilities to the community. There has been very prominent figures on the history who had got the education in Madressa. But looking at the present context, this system needs an overhaul. There are some problems like poor infrastructure, lack of coordination between mainstream and Madressa education, avoidance of science and mathematics etc...

M2 : One university has been named as Banaras Hindu University. There is also Aligarh Muslim University. Do you think this is proper? Shall we name Universities like this?

Me: Sir we have to see the historical context behind this. These institutions were established in a period when some reasons existed. For example Aligarh Muslim University was established by Sir Sayed Ahmed Khan to spread education among Muslims so that they can compete with other communities in employment and other areas. But if we see in present context when we have adopted a secular Constitution, I don't see any need of that.

M2: Safin you might have heard about the role of these Deras and their influence on society. Even there are dectates from religious leaders and also it is in Islam. How these can impact society??

Me: Sir, in India relious identity is very strong. Everyone wants to be associated with religion. If we talk about Deras, they have provided equality in lower strata of society and a feeling of being in the main stream. They have also given psychological support to these people and hence they follow what their religious teacher tell them. Similar is the case with Fatwa in Islam. If we involve these leaders in political consultation over societal issues, it can impact society at large.

(M2 passing to M3)

M3: okay Hasan, (Chairman interrupted, "It's Safin")
Yeah right, Safin... There is a prohibition in Gujarat on Alcohol. But we all know that it's available. Just you have to pay bit more for that. So what do you think about this prohibition...

Me: Yes sir , Gujarat being the birth place of our father of nation, it has implemented a ban on Alcohol since the day one. But I think instead of going for blanket ban, we should try for spreading awareness about negative consequences of alcohol consumption and sensitization. Behavioral change is all what is needed. We can also take help from the religious leaders as we have discussed earlier.

M3 : but this prohibition has also gained support from women. In state like Bihar, they have implemented it for political scores. Do you think this prohibition or removing it can have negative impact on political parties?

Me: Yes sir, prohibition or removal of it do have the political consequences.

(Passing to M4)

M4: Safin, you have done electronics. Can we develop an app to curb the corruption in your District? 

Me: Sir ,even the existing apps like WhatsApp can also be used for that. I can ask the citizens to reach to me over such issues and if I find any substance in the complaint, I would go into details if that case. Secondly, yes developing an app and reducing the manual contact between an officer and citizen would result in a lower level of corruption.

M4:  There has been a case of gender divide as well as rural - urban divide. I'm sure that is the case in your state too. How will reduce this divide using IT and cyber technology.?

Me: Yes sir, in Gujarat we have this rural urban divide. For me the priority would be internet penetration in rural areas. Focus on e-govern
ance would also empower the rural citizens. Apart from that some critical services like telemedicine and tele-education would also help to bridge the gap.

M4: We have heard about cyber threats. Wheta are they? Do you think we should try to avoid the technology to save ourselves from the threat??
 
Me:  Sir the biggest threat is about privacy of an individual and security of data. Like very recently we have seen this Facebook data theft. But abandoning a tachnology is not a wise decision. We should work on robust data policy and cyber security instead.

M4: Safin, literature is your optional. Do you know Hansa Mehta? What has been here contribution in Gujarati.?

Me: Yes sir, I have heard about her and she had also played a role in constintuition making. But sorry sir, I'm not aware about her contribution in Gujarati.

M4: no issues. Last question. There is very well known personality from Gujarat who is internationally recognized as a successful businessman. Can you tell.me?

Me: Sir , I think you are talking about Mr Dhirubhai Ambani.

M4: Yes yes... He stayed outside the country for many years and then he started business here. Can you name the country where he had stayed??

Me : Sorry sir I am not aware about it.

M4: It's Aden. Thank you.

Chairman: (She was very attentive throughout and often smiled )Safin, I think you seem to know a lot. You have answered all the questions very promptly. Tell me what you still feel that you should learn...

Me: (with smile) ma'am I still need to learn a lot 

Chairman : (interrupted me). See, even you know this also that what you still need to learn. That's a positive thing indeed. Plz continue...

Me: ma'am I need to learn about many sports. In my childhood i couldn't get engaged in any sports because I had responsibilities and also had to take care of my younger brother as both my parents were engaged in labour work. Apart from that, I am very much interested in Constitution and I am studying on that also.

Chairman: Being an IAS , which state would you like to work in...

Me: I have filled Gujarat as my home state and being my first preference I would like to work there.

M3 : Do you know what is the disadvantage of that?

Me: yes sir, in that case your family members, relatives and friends expect a lot from you and you have to struggles with that.

(All members laughing )
M3: you have given very correct point...

Chairman: okay Safin tell me, If you get into IAS, how it will help you to improve?

Me: first of all, I would get into touch with intellectual class of the country and that would help me to build my thought process. IAS being a post dealing with vast no of subject will increase my knowledge, my critical thinking and decisiveness.

M3: Tell me one thing, do your coachings tell you to write such hobbies?? Dont worry, it's a normal think. Everyone needs a coaching and that's completely fine. Bit people write like helping blinds and somebody write cooking... N yours is also.quite different.... So do they tell you ??

Me: Sir, I have attended coaching but the hobby which I have mentioned , I have genuinely done work in that area for around 4 years during my college.

M3: Thats good.

Have a good day to all.
